questions.question: One of the factors of (8 2k + 5 2k ), where k is an odd number, is:
questions.questionHtml: One of the factors of (8<sup>2k</sup> + 5<sup>2k</sup>), where k is an odd number, is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Expression = 82k + 52k

k = odd number

Formula used:

an + bn is divisible by (a + b) when n is odd

Calculation:

\(8^{2k} + 5^{2k} = (8^2)^k + (5^2)^k\)

⇒ \(64^k + 25^k\)

⇒ Factor = 64 + 25

⇒ Factor = 89

∴ The correct answer is option (2).

questions.question: \({\left( {\frac{{1 - tan\theta }}{{1 - \cot \theta }}} \right)^2} + 1 = ?\)
questions.questionHtml: \({\left( {\frac{{1 - tan\theta }}{{1 - \cot \theta }}} \right)^2} + 1 = ?\)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Substitute θ = 60°, so tan 60° = √3 and cot 60° = 1/√3.

Expression = ((1 − √3) / (1 − 1/√3))2 + 1

= ((1 − √3) / ((√3 − 1)/√3))2 + 1 = (−√3)2 + 1 = 3 + 1 = 4.

Checking options: sec2 60° = (2)2 = 4. Other options do not match.

∴ The correct answer is sec2 θ.

Alternate Method

Given: ((1 − tanθ) / (1 − cotθ))2 + 1

Formula used: tanθ = sinθ/cosθ, cotθ = cosθ/sinθ, 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ

⇒ ((1 − sinθ/cosθ) / (1 − cosθ/sinθ))2 + 1

⇒ (((cosθ − sinθ) / cosθ) / ((sinθ − cosθ) / sinθ))2 + 1

⇒ ((cosθ − sinθ) / cosθ × sinθ / (sinθ − cosθ))2 + 1

⇒ (−sinθ / cosθ)2 + 1

⇒ (−tanθ)2 + 1

⇒ tan2θ + 1

⇒ sec2θ

∴ The correct answer is sec2 θ.

Additional Information

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental relations in trigonometry: sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ, and 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ.

Reciprocal Relations

Basic reciprocal properties: tanθ = 1/cotθ, sinθ = 1/cosecθ, and cosθ = 1/secθ.

Ratio Formulas

Expressed in terms of sine and cosine: tanθ = sinθ/cosθ and cotθ = cosθ/sinθ.

questions.question: In what ratio, sugar costing Rs. 60 per kg be mixed with sugar costing Rs. 42 per kg such that by selling the mixture at Rs. 56 per kg there is a gain of 12%?
questions.questionHtml: In what ratio, sugar costing Rs. 60 per kg be mixed with sugar costing Rs. 42 per kg such that by selling the mixture at Rs. 56 per kg there is a gain of 12%?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Step 1: Calculate the Cost Price (CP) of the mixture from Selling Price (SP) and Profit%.

CP of mixture = (SP × 100) / (100 + Profit%) = (56 × 100) / 112 = ₹50/kg.

Step 2: Apply Alligation Rule: Ratio = (Mean CP − Lower CP) : (Higher CP − Mean CP).

Ratio = (50 − 42) : (60 − 50) = 8 : 10 = 4 : 5.

∴ The correct answer is 4 : 5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost of sugar 1 (CP1) = ₹60/kg

Cost of sugar 2 (CP2) = ₹42/kg

Selling price of mixture (SPm) = ₹56/kg

Profit percentage = 12%

Formula Used:

Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 / (100 + Gain%)

Alligation Rule: (Quantity of Cheaper) / (Quantity of Dearer) = (CP of Dearer − Mean CP) / (Mean CP − CP of Cheaper)

Calculations:

⇒ Mean Cost Price = 56 × 100 / (100 + 12)

⇒ Mean Cost Price = 5600 / 112 = ₹50/kg

⇒ Applying Alligation: (Sugar 1 Quantity) : (Sugar 2 Quantity)

⇒ Ratio = (Mean CP − CP2) : (CP1 − Mean CP)

⇒ Ratio = (50 − 42) : (60 − 50)

⇒ Ratio = 8 : 10

⇒ Ratio = 4 : 5

∴ The correct answer is 4 : 5.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation

It is used to find the ratio in which two or more ingredients at their respective prices must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired price. Ratio = (Price of dearer − Mean price) : (Mean price − Price of cheaper).

Cost Price vs Selling Price

Always ensure all values used in the alligation cross are of the same type (all Cost Prices or all Selling Prices). If a profit is given on the mixture, convert SP to CP first.

Applications of Alligation

This method can be applied to mixtures of liquids, averages of marks, speed-time-distance problems, and calculating interest rates on parts of a principal.

questions.question: The value of \(\frac{{7 + 8 \times 8 \div 8\;of\;8 + 8 \div 8 \times 4\;of\;4}}{{4 \div 4\;of\;4 + 4 \times 4 \div 4 - 4 \div 4\;of\;2}}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\frac{{7 + 8 \times 8 \div 8\;of\;8 + 8 \div 8 \times 4\;of\;4}}{{4 \div 4\;of\;4 + 4 \times 4 \div 4 - 4 \div 4\;of\;2}}\) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{7 + 8 \times 8 \div 8\;of\;8 + 8 \div 8 \times 4\;of\;4}{4 \div 4\;of\;4 + 4 \times 4 \div 4 - 4 \div 4\;of\;2}\)

Formula used:

VBODMAS Rule

Calculation:

Numerator = 7 + 8 × 8 ÷ (8 of 8) + 8 ÷ 8 × (4 of 4)

⇒ Numerator = 7 + 8 × 8 ÷ 64 + 8 ÷ 8 × 16

⇒ Numerator = 7 + 64 ÷ 64 + 1 × 16

⇒ Numerator = 7 + 1 + 16 = 24

Denominator = 4 ÷ (4 of 4) + 4 × 4 ÷ 4 - 4 ÷ (4 of 2)

⇒ Denominator = 4 ÷ 16 + 16 ÷ 4 - 4 ÷ 8

⇒ Denominator = 0.25 + 4 - 0.5 = 3.75

Value = 24 ÷ 3.75

⇒ Value = 6.4

∴ The correct answer is option (2).

questions.question: The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 1/7 of the number. The units digit is 4 less than the tens digit. If the number obtained on reversing its digits is divided by 7, the remainder will be:
questions.questionHtml: The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 1/7 of the number. The units digit is 4 less than the tens digit. If the number obtained on reversing its digits is divided by 7, the remainder will be:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of number to sum of digits is 7 : 1 ⇒ 10x + y = 7(x + y) ⇒ 3x = 6y ⇒ x = 2y.

Given that units digit (y) is 4 less than tens digit (x), so x − y = 4.

Substituting x = 2y: 2y − y = 4 ⇒ y = 4 and x = 8. The number is 84.

Reversing 84 gives 48. Now divide 48 by 7: 48 = (7 × 6) + 6.

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Alternate Method

Given:

Sum of digits = 1/7 × (Two-digit number)

Units digit = Tens digit − 4

Formula Used:

A two-digit number with tens digit x and units digit y is expressed as 10x + y.

⇒ Let the tens digit be x and the units digit be y.

⇒ According to the first condition: x + y = (10x + y) ÷ 7

⇒ 7(x + y) = 10x + y ⇒ 7x + 7y = 10x + y

⇒ 3x = 6y ⇒ x = 2y ... (Eq. 1)

⇒ According to the second condition: y = x − 4 ⇒ x − y = 4 ... (Eq. 2)

⇒ Substitute Eq. 1 into Eq. 2: 2y − y = 4 ⇒ y = 4

⇒ x = 2 × 4 = 8

⇒ The original number = 10(8) + 4 = 84

⇒ The reversed number = 10(4) + 8 = 48

⇒ Dividing reversed number by 7: 48 ÷ 7 = 6 with a remainder of 6.

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Additional Information

Two-Digit Number Properties

A 2-digit number 10x+y and its reverse 10y+x always have a difference that is a multiple of 9, i.e., |(10x+y) − (10y+x)| = 9|x−y|.

Divisibility and Remainders

For any number N divided by d, N = dq + r, where q is the quotient and 0 ≤ r < d is the remainder.

Sum of Digits Rule

If a number is a multiple of its digit sum, such as 84 being 7 × 12, it often relates to divisibility rules of 3 or 9.

questions.question: In ΔABC, AB = 7, BC = 10 cm, and AC = 8 cm. If AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC, where D is a point on BC, then BD is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, AB = 7, BC = 10 cm, and AC = 8 cm. If AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC, where D is a point on BC, then BD is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

According to the Angle Bisector Theorem, the ratio of the segments formed on the opposite side is equal to the ratio of the other two sides.

Ratio BD : DC = AB : AC = 7 : 8

Total ratio parts = 7 + 8 = 15 units

Given total length BC = 10 cm

BD = (7 ÷ 15) × 10 = 14/3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 14/3 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: AB = 7 cm, AC = 8 cm, BC = 10 cm. AD is the internal bisector of ∠BAC.

Formula Used: In ΔABC, if AD bisects ∠A, then BD / DC = AB / AC.

Let BD = x cm. Then DC = (10 − x) cm.

⇒ BD / DC = AB / AC

⇒ x / (10 − x) = 7 / 8

⇒ 8 × x = 7 × (10 − x)

⇒ 8x = 70 − 7x

⇒ 8x + 7x = 70

⇒ 15x = 70

⇒ x = 70 ÷ 15

⇒ x = 14/3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 14/3 cm.

Additional Information

Internal Angle Bisector Theorem

The bisector of an interior angle of a triangle divides the opposite side internally in the ratio of the sides containing the angle. BD/DC = AB/AC.

External Angle Bisector Theorem

The bisector of an exterior angle of a triangle divides the opposite side externally in the ratio of the sides containing the angle. BE/CE = AB/AC.

Length of the Bisector

The length of the internal angle bisector AD can be calculated using the formula AD2 = AB × AC − BD × DC.

Incenter of a Triangle

The intersection point of all three internal angle bisectors is called the incenter, which is the center of the circle inscribed in the triangle.

questions.question: Raghav spends 80% of his income. If his income increases by 12% and the savings decrease by 10%, then what will be the percentage increase in his expenditure?
questions.questionHtml: Raghav spends 80% of his income. If his income increases by 12% and the savings decrease by 10%, then what will be the percentage increase in his expenditure?
questions.solution:
Let the income of raghav be Rs. x

His expenditure = x × (80/100) = 0.80x

His savings = x – 0.8x = 0.2x

If his income increase by 12%, then his new income = x × (112/100) = 1.12x

If his savings decreased by 10%, then his new savings = 0.2x × (90/100) = 0.18x

His new expenditure = 1.12x – 0.18x = 0.94x

His expenditure increased by = 0.94x – 0.80x = 0.14x

His expenditure increased by (in%) = (0.14x/0.80x) × 100 = 17.5

questions.question: PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral in which PQ = 14.4 cm, QR = 12.8 cm and SR = 9.6 cm. If PR bisects QS, what is the length of PS?
questions.questionHtml: PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral in which PQ = 14.4 cm, QR = 12.8 cm and SR = 9.6 cm. If PR bisects QS, what is the length of PS?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a cyclic quadrilateral, if one diagonal bisects the other, the product of the adjacent sides of the bisecting diagonal is equal.

If PR bisects QS, then the property is: PQ × QR = PS × SR

Given: PQ = 14.4 cm, QR = 12.8 cm, SR = 9.6 cm

⇒ 14.4 × 12.8 = PS × 9.6

⇒ PS = (14.4 × 12.8) ÷ 9.6 = 1.5 × 12.8 = 19.2 cm

∴ The correct answer is 19.2 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

PQ = 14.4 cm, QR = 12.8 cm, SR = 9.6 cm

Diagonal PR bisects diagonal QS at point O (QO = OS).

Formula Used:

In a cyclic quadrilateral PQRS, if diagonal PR bisects QS, then Area(ΔPQR) = Area(ΔPSR).

⇒ 1/2 × PQ × QR × sin(Q) = 1/2 × PS × SR × sin(S)

Since ∠Q + ∠S = 180° (Cyclic quadrilateral property), sin(Q) = sin(S).

⇒ PQ × QR = PS × SR

Calculations:

⇒ 14.4 × 12.8 = PS × 9.6

⇒ PS = (14.4 × 12.8) ÷ 9.6

⇒ PS = 184.32 ÷ 9.6

⇒ PS = 19.2 cm

∴ The correct answer is 19.2 cm.

Additional Information

Cyclic Quadrilateral Definition

A quadrilateral whose all four vertices lie on the circumference of a circle. Sum of opposite angles is always 180° (∠P + ∠R = 180°).

Ptolemy's Theorem

In a cyclic quadrilateral, the product of the diagonals is equal to the sum of the products of opposite sides: (PR × QS) = (PQ × RS) + (PS × QR).

Area of Cyclic Quadrilateral

Area = √((s−a)(s−b)(s−c)(s−d)), where s is the semi-perimeter (a+b+c+d)/2. This is known as Brahmagupta's Formula.

questions.question: The ratio of copper to zinc in alloys A and B are 3 : 4 and 5 : 9 respectively. A and B are taken in the ratio 2 : 3 and melted to form a new alloy C. What is the ratio of copper to zinc in C?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of copper to zinc in alloys A and B are 3 : 4 and 5 : 9 respectively. A and B are taken in the ratio 2 : 3 and melted to form a new alloy C. What is the ratio of copper to zinc in C?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total parts in A = 3 + 4 = 7; Total parts in B = 5 + 9 = 14.

Equalize parts by multiplying Alloy A ratio by 2: A → 6 : 8 (Total 14).

Now multiply by mixing ratio 2 : 3:

A → (6 × 2) : (8 × 2) = 12 : 16; B → (5 × 3) : (9 × 3) = 15 : 27.

New Copper = 12 + 15 = 27; New Zinc = 16 + 27 = 43.

∴ The correct answer is 27 : 43.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of Cu:Zn in A = 3 : 4

Ratio of Cu:Zn in B = 5 : 9

Mixing ratio A : B = 2 : 3

Calculations:

⇒ Fraction of Copper in A = 3/7 and Zinc in A = 4/7

⇒ Fraction of Copper in B = 5/14 and Zinc in B = 9/14

⇒ Total Copper in C = (2 × 3/7) + (3 × 5/14)

⇒ Total Copper in C = 6/7 + 15/14 = (12 + 15)/14 = 27/14

⇒ Total Zinc in C = (2 × 4/7) + (3 × 9/14)

⇒ Total Zinc in C = 8/7 + 27/14 = (16 + 27)/14 = 43/14

⇒ Required Ratio = (27/14) : (43/14) = 27 : 43

∴ The correct answer is 27 : 43.

Additional Information

Alligation Rule for Mixtures

Quantity of cheaper / Quantity of dearer = (Rate of dearer − Mean rate) / (Mean rate − Rate of cheaper).

Weighted Average Formula

Average = (n1x1 + n2x2) / (n1 + n2), where n represents quantities and x represents values/ratios.

Ratio Balancing

To combine ratios of different totals, find the LCM of the sums of the parts and multiply each ratio accordingly to equalize the base.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 18,000 is lent at 10% p.a compound interest, compounded annually, what is the difference between the compound interest for 3 rd year and 4 th year?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 18,000 is lent at 10% p.a compound interest, compounded annually, what is the difference between the compound interest for 3<sup>rd</sup> year and 4<sup>th</sup> year?
questions.solution:
P = 18,000, r = 10% and t = 2 years, then

A = P (1 + r/100)2

A = 18,000 (1 + 10/100)2 = 18,000 × (11/10) × (11/10) = 21,780

So, Compound interest for 3rd year = 21780 × (10/100) = 2178

Amount will be after 3 year = 21780 + 2178 = 23958

So, compound interest for 4th year = 22958 × (10/100) = 2395.8

So, Difference of compound interest for 3rd year and 4th year = 2395.8 – 2178 = 217.80

questions.question: A and B started their journeys from X to Y and Y to X, respectively. After crossing each other, A and B completed the remaining parts of their journeys in \(6\frac{1}{8}\) h and 8 h respectively. If the speed of B is 28 km/h, then the speed (in km/h) of A is:
questions.questionHtml: A and B started their journeys from X to Y and Y to X, respectively. After crossing each other, A and B completed the remaining parts of their journeys in \(6\frac{1}{8}\) h and 8 h respectively. If the speed of B is 28 km/h, then the speed (in km/h) of A is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For two objects starting from opposite ends and moving towards each other, if they meet and then take times T1 and T2 to reach their respective destinations, the ratio of their speeds is S1/S2 = √(T2/T1).

Given: T1 = 6 (1/8) h = 49/8 h, T2 = 8 h, and S2 (Speed of B) = 28 km/h.

Ratio of speeds SA/SB = √(8 / (49/8)) = √(64/49) = 8/7.

Speed of A = (8/7) × Speed of B = (8/7) × 28 = 8 × 4 = 32 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 32 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of B (SB) = 28 km/h

Time taken by A after crossing (TA) = 6 (1/8) = 49/8 hours

Time taken by B after crossing (TB) = 8 hours

Formula:

SA / SB = √(TB / TA)

Calculations:

⇒ SA / 28 = √(8 / (49/8))

⇒ SA / 28 = √(8 × 8 / 49)

⇒ SA / 28 = √(64 / 49)

⇒ SA / 28 = 8 / 7

⇒ SA = (8 / 7) × 28

⇒ SA = 8 × 4

⇒ SA = 32 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 32 km/h.

Additional Information

Meeting Time Formula

In cases where two objects start simultaneously and meet, then take T1 and T2 times to reach the ends, the time from the start until they meet is given by T = √(T1 × T2).

Relative Speed

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S1 + S2).

Speed-Time Relation

For a fixed distance, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T), but in these specific meeting-point problems, the square root relationship is derived from equating the time taken to reach the meeting point.

questions.question: If θ lies in the first quadrant and cos 2 θ – sin 2 θ = 1/2 then the value of tan 2 2θ + sin 2 3θ is:
questions.questionHtml: If θ lies in the first quadrant and cos<sup>2</sup>θ – sin<sup>2</sup>θ = 1/2 then the value of tan<sup>2</sup>2θ + sin<sup>2</sup>3θ is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given: cos2θ − sin2θ = 1/2

Use Identity: cos 2θ = cos2θ − sin2θ

∴ cos 2θ = 1/2 ⇒ 2θ = 60° (θ = 30°)

Value = tan2(60°) + sin2(3 × 30°)

Value = (√3)2 + (1)2 = 3 + 1 = 4

∴ The correct answer is 4.

Alternate Method

Given:

cos2θ − sin2θ = 1/2

θ is in the first quadrant (0° < θ < 90°)

Formula Used:

1. cos 2θ = cos2θ − sin2θ

2. tan 60° = √3

3. sin 90° = 1

Calculations:

⇒ cos2θ − sin2θ = 1/2

⇒ cos 2θ = 1/2

⇒ 2θ = cos−1(1/2)

⇒ 2θ = 60°

⇒ θ = 30°

Now, substitute the values in the required expression:

⇒ tan22θ + sin23θ

⇒ tan2(60°) + sin2(3 × 30°)

⇒ tan2(60°) + sin2(90°)

⇒ (√3)2 + (1)2

⇒ 3 + 1 = 4

∴ The correct answer is 4.

Additional Information

Double Angle Identities

cos 2θ can also be written as 2cos2θ − 1 or 1 − 2sin2θ. Similarly, sin 2θ = 2sinθcosθ.

Pythagorean Identity

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1. This can be used to convert cos2θ − sin2θ into terms of only sin or cos.

Common Trig Values

For 30°: sin = 1/2, cos = √3/2, tan = 1/√3. For 60°: sin = √3/2, cos = 1/2, tan = √3.

questions.question: If x + y + z = 11, x 2 + y 2 + z 2 = 133 and x 3 + y 3 + z 3 = 881, then the value of ∛(xyz) is:
questions.questionHtml: If x + y + z = 11, x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + z<sup>2</sup> = 133 and x<sup>3</sup> + y<sup>3</sup> + z<sup>3</sup> = 881, then the value of ∛(xyz) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Find (xy + yz + zx) = [(x + y + z)2 − (x2 + y2 + z2)] ÷ 2 = [121 − 133] ÷ 2 = −6.

Find 3xyz = (x3 + y3 + z3) − (x + y + z)[(x2 + y2 + z2) − (xy + yz + zx)]

3xyz = 881 − 11[133 − (−6)] = 881 − 11(139) = 881 − 1529 = −648.

xyz = −648 ÷ 3 = −216.

∛(xyz) = ∛(−216) = −6.

∴ The correct answer is -6.

Alternate Method

Given:

x + y + z = 11

x2 + y2 + z2 = 133

x3 + y3 + z3 = 881

Formula Used:

1) (x + y + z)2 = x2 + y2 + z2 + 2(xy + yz + zx)

2) x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x2 + y2 + z2 − (xy + yz + zx))

Calculations:

⇒ (11)2 = 133 + 2(xy + yz + zx)

⇒ 121 − 133 = 2(xy + yz + zx)

⇒ −12 = 2(xy + yz + zx)

⇒ xy + yz + zx = −6

⇒ 881 − 3xyz = 11 × [133 − (−6)]

⇒ 881 − 3xyz = 11 × 139

⇒ 881 − 3xyz = 1529

⇒ −3xyz = 1529 − 881

⇒ −3xyz = 648

⇒ xyz = −216

⇒ ∛(xyz) = ∛(−216) = −6

∴ The correct answer is -6.

Additional Information

Sum of Cubes Identity

The identity x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x2 + y2 + z2 − xy − yz − zx) is fundamental in algebra. If x + y + z = 0, then x3 + y3 + z3 = 3xyz.

Alternative Form of Identity

The term (x2 + y2 + z2 − xy − yz − zx) can also be written as ½[(x−y)2 + (y−z)2 + (z−x)2].

Square of Trinomial

(x + y + z)2 = x2 + y2 + z2 + 2(xy + yz + zx) helps in finding the sum of products taken two at a time when the sum of squares and sum of variables are known.

questions.question: A right circular cylinder of the maximum volume is cut out from a solid wooden cube. The material left is what percent of the volume (nearest to an integer) of the original cube?
questions.questionHtml: A right circular cylinder of the maximum volume is cut out from a solid wooden cube. The material left is what percent of the volume (nearest to an integer) of the original cube?
questions.solution:
Let the side of the cube be a cm.

As we know,

Volume of cube = a3

Volume of cylinder = πr2h

Then radius of cylinder = a/2

Height of the cylinder (h) = a

Volume of cylinder = πr2h = π × (a/2)2 × a = 3.14a3/4 = 0.785a3

Volume of waste = a3 – 0.785a3 = 0.215a3

Volume of waste percentage = [0.215a3/a3] × 100 = 21% (approx)

questions.question: If the radius of the base of a cone is doubled, and the volume of the new cone is three times the volume of the original cone, then what will be the ratio of the height of the original cone to that of the new cone?
questions.questionHtml: If the radius of the base of a cone is doubled, and the volume of the new cone is three times the volume of the original cone, then what will be the ratio of the height of the original cone to that of the new cone?
questions.solution:
Let the radius of the cone be r cm and height of the cone be h1 cm, then

Volume of cone = (1/3) × πr2h1 = (πr2h1)/3

If the radius of the base of the cone is doubled, and let the height of the new cone be h2

Volume of new cone = (1/3) × π × (2r)2 × h2 = 4(πr2h2)/3

According to the question

⇒ [(πr2h1)/3] / [4(πr2h2)/3] = 1/3

⇒ h1/h2 = 4/3

Required ratio h1: h2 = 4 : 3

questions.question: When 7897, 8110 and 8536 are divided by the greatest number x, then the remainder in each case is the same. The sum of the digits of x is:
questions.questionHtml: When 7897, 8110 and 8536 are divided by the greatest number x, then the remainder in each case is the same. The sum of the digits of x is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When the remainder is the same, the greatest number x is the HCF of the differences between the numbers.

Difference 1 = 8110 − 7897 = 213

Difference 2 = 8536 − 8110 = 426

x = HCF(213, 426) = 213

Sum of digits of x = 2 + 1 + 3 = 6

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Alternate Method

Given:

Numbers: 7897, 8110, 8536

Formula used:

If numbers a, b, and c leave the same remainder when divided by x, then x = HCF(|a−b|, |b−c|, |c−a|).

⇒ Difference 1 = 8110 − 7897 = 213

⇒ Difference 2 = 8536 − 8110 = 426

⇒ Difference 3 = 8536 − 7897 = 639

⇒ x = HCF(213, 426, 639)

⇒ 213 = 213 × 1

⇒ 426 = 213 × 2

⇒ 639 = 213 × 3

⇒ x = 213

⇒ Sum of digits of x = 2 + 1 + 3 = 6

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Additional Information

HCF with Same Remainder

When the remainder is the same but unknown, calculate the HCF of the absolute differences between the given numbers: HCF(|a−b|, |b−c|, |c−a|).

HCF with Known Remainder

If dividing a, b, and c leaves remainder r, the greatest number is HCF(a−r, b−r, c−r).

LCM with Same Remainder

The smallest number which when divided by a, b, and c leaves a remainder r in each case is given by: LCM(a, b, c) + r.

questions.question: In a constituency, 55% of the total number of voters are males and the rest are females. If 40% of the males are illiterate and 40% of the females are literate, then by what percent is the number of literate males more than that of illiterate females?
questions.questionHtml: In a constituency, 55% of the total number of voters are males and the rest are females. If 40% of the males are illiterate and 40% of the females are literate, then by what percent is the number of literate males more than that of illiterate females?
questions.solution:
Let total number of person in the constituency be 100x

Number of male in the constituency = 100x × (55/100) = 55x

Number of female in the constituency = 100x – 55x = 45x

Number of illiterate males in the constituency = 55x × (40/100) = 22

Number of literate males = 55x – 22x = 33x

Number of literate females = 45 × (40/100) = 18x

Number of illiterate females = 45x – 18x = 27x

Number of literate males more than of illiterate females by = 33x – 27x = 6x

Number of literate males more than that of illiterate females by (in%) = (6x/27x) × 100 = 22\(\frac{2}{9}{\rm{\% }}\)

questions.question: Let a, b and c be the fractions such that a < b < c. If c is divided by a, the result is 5/2, which exceeds b by 7/4, If \(a + b + c = 1\frac{{11}}{{12}},\) then (c – a) will be equal to:
questions.questionHtml: Let a, b and c be the fractions such that a < b < c. If c is divided by a, the result is 5/2, which exceeds b by 7/4, If \(a + b + c = 1\frac{{11}}{{12}},\) then (c – a) will be equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

Fractions a, b, and c where a < b < c

\(\frac{c}{a} = \frac{5}{2}\)

\(\frac{c}{a} - b = \frac{7}{4}\)

\(a + b + c = 1\frac{11}{12} = \frac{23}{12}\)

Formula used:

Algebraic Substitution

Calculation:

\(\frac{5}{2} - b = \frac{7}{4}\)

⇒ \(b = \frac{5}{2} - \frac{7}{4}\)

⇒ \(b = \frac{10 - 7}{4} = \frac{3}{4}\)

Substitute b and c = \(\frac{5a}{2}\) into a + b + c = \(\frac{23}{12}\)

⇒ \(a + \frac{3}{4} + \frac{5a}{2} = \frac{23}{12}\)

⇒ \(\frac{7a}{2} = \frac{23}{12} - \frac{3}{4}\)

⇒ \(\frac{7a}{2} = \frac{23 - 9}{12}\)

⇒ \(\frac{7a}{2} = \frac{14}{12} = \frac{7}{6}\)

⇒ \(a = \frac{7}{6} \times \frac{2}{7} = \frac{1}{3}\)

⇒ \(c = \frac{5}{2} \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{5}{6}\)

Calculation for (c - a):

⇒ \(c - a = \frac{5}{6} - \frac{1}{3}\)

⇒ \(c - a = \frac{5 - 2}{6} = \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}\)

∴ The correct answer is option (4).

questions.question: If the radius of a right circular cylinder is decreased by 20% while its height is increased by 40% then the percentage change in its volume will be by:
questions.questionHtml: If the radius of a right circular cylinder is decreased by 20% while its height is increased by 40% then the percentage change in its volume will be by:
questions.solution:
Let the radius of the cylinder be r cm and height of the cylinder be h cm

As we know,

Volume of the cylinder = πr2h

If radius of the cylinder decreased by 20%, then new radius of the cylinder = r × (80/100) = 0.8r

If height of the cylinder increased by 40% then new height of the cylinder = h × (140/100) = 1.4h

New volume of the cylinder = π (0.8r)2 × 1.4 = 0.896πr2h

Volume decreased by = πr2h – 0.896πr2h = 0.104πr2h

Volume decreased by (in %) = [0.104πr2h/πr2h] × 100 = 10.4%

questions.question: The base of the right prism is a trapezium whose parallel sides are 11 cm and 15 cm and the distance between them is 9 cm. If the volume of the prism is 1731.6 cm 3 , then the height (in cm) of the prism will be:
questions.questionHtml: The base of the right prism is a trapezium whose parallel sides are 11 cm and 15 cm and the distance between them is 9 cm. If the volume of the prism is 1731.6 cm<sup>3</sup>, then the height (in cm) of the prism will be:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Base Area of Trapezium = 1/2 × (11 + 15) × 9 = 13 × 9 = 117 cm2

Volume of Prism = Base Area × Height

Height = 1731.6 ÷ 117 = 14.8 cm

∴ The correct answer is 14.8 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Parallel sides of trapezium base (a) = 11 cm, (b) = 15 cm

Distance between parallel sides (hb) = 9 cm

Volume of prism (V) = 1731.6 cm3

Formula Used:

Area of Trapezium = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Distance between them

Volume of Prism = Area of Base × Height of Prism (H)

Calculations:

⇒ Area of the trapezium base = 1/2 × (11 + 15) × 9

⇒ Area of the trapezium base = 1/2 × 26 × 9

⇒ Area of the trapezium base = 13 × 9 = 117 cm2

⇒ Volume of the prism = Area of base × Height

⇒ 1731.6 = 117 × H

⇒ H = 1731.6 ÷ 117

⇒ H = 14.8 cm

∴ The correct answer is 14.8 cm.

Additional Information

Volume of a Right Prism

The volume is always calculated as the area of the base multiplied by the vertical height (V = Base Area × H).

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) of Prism

The LSA of a prism is given by the perimeter of the base multiplied by the height (LSA = Perimeter of base × H).

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Prism

The TSA includes the lateral area and the area of the two bases (TSA = LSA + 2 × Base Area).

Area of Trapezium

Area = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × h, where h is the perpendicular distance between parallel sides.

questions.question: If each interior angle of a regular polygon is \({\left( {128\frac{4}{7}} \right)}\) °, then what is the sum of the number of its diagonals and the number of its sides?
questions.questionHtml: If each interior angle of a regular polygon is \({\left( {128\frac{4}{7}} \right)}\)°,  then what is the sum of the number of its diagonals and the number of its sides?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Interior angle = 128 4/7° = 900/7°

Exterior angle = 180° − 900/7° = 360/7°

Number of sides (n) = 360° ÷ Exterior angle = 360 ÷ (360/7) = 7

Number of diagonals = n(n − 3) ÷ 2 = 7 × 4 ÷ 2 = 14

Sum = Diagonals + Sides = 14 + 7 = 21

∴ The correct answer is 21.

Alternate Method

Given: Each interior angle = 128 4/7°

Formula Used:

1. Interior Angle + Exterior Angle = 180°

2. Number of sides (n) = 360° ÷ Exterior Angle

3. Number of diagonals = n(n − 3) ÷ 2

⇒ Interior angle = (128 × 7 + 4) / 7 = 900/7°

⇒ Exterior angle = 180° − 900/7°

⇒ Exterior angle = (1260 − 900) / 7 = 360/7°

⇒ Number of sides (n) = 360° ÷ (360/7°) = 7

⇒ Number of diagonals = 7 × (7 − 3) ÷ 2

⇒ Number of diagonals = 7 × 4 ÷ 2 = 14

⇒ Required Sum = Sides + Diagonals = 7 + 14 = 21

∴ The correct answer is 21.

Additional Information

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of a polygon with n sides is given by (n − 2) × 180°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

For any convex polygon, the sum of all exterior angles (one at each vertex) is always 360°.

Relationship between Angles

In a regular polygon, each interior angle = [(n − 2) × 180°] / n and each exterior angle = 360° / n.

Polygon Diagonals

A triangle (n=3) has 0 diagonals. A quadrilateral (n=4) has 2 diagonals. The general formula is n(n−3)/2.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 8,400 amounts to Rs. 11,046 at 8.75% p.a simple interest in a certain time. What is the simple interest on the sum of Rs. 9,600 at the same rate for the same time?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 8,400 amounts to Rs. 11,046 at 8.75% p.a simple interest in a certain time. What is the simple interest on the sum of Rs. 9,600 at the same rate for the same time?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Interest SI1 = 11,046 − 8,400 = Rs. 2,646

Since Rate and Time are constant, Simple Interest is directly proportional to Principal (SI ∝ P).

Ratio of Principals = 8,400 : 9,600 = 7 : 8

New Interest SI2 = (2,646 ÷ 7) × 8

SI2 = 378 × 8 = Rs. 3,024

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,024.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P1) = Rs. 8,400, Amount (A1) = Rs. 11,046, Rate (R) = 8.75%

Second Principal (P2) = Rs. 9,600, Rate and Time are same as Case 1.

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

Calculations:

⇒ SI1 = A1 − P1 = 11,046 − 8,400 = 2,646

⇒ Time (T) = (SI1 × 100) ÷ (P1 × R)

⇒ T = (2,646 × 100) ÷ (8,400 × 8.75)

⇒ T = 2,646 ÷ (84 × 8.75)

⇒ New SI (SI2) = (P2 × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ SI2 = (9,600 × 8.75 × [2,646 ÷ (84 × 8.75)]) ÷ 100

⇒ SI2 = (96 × 8.75 × 2,646) ÷ (84 × 8.75)

⇒ SI2 = (96 × 2,646) ÷ 84

⇒ SI2 = (8 × 2,646) ÷ 7

⇒ SI2 = 8 × 378 = 3,024

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,024.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Proportionality

When the Rate (R) and Time (T) are constant, Simple Interest is directly proportional to the Principal (SI ∝ P). This allows for quick calculation using ratios: SI1/P1 = SI2/P2.

Effective Rate of Interest

The total interest earned can be expressed as an effective percentage of the principal, which is (Rate × Time)%. For Simple Interest, this percentage remains linear over time.

SI vs CI Difference

For a period of 1 year with annual compounding, SI and CI are equal. The difference for 2 years is given by P × (R/100)2.

questions.question: If a 2 + b 2 + c 2 + 96 = 8(a + b – 2c), then √(ab – bc + ca) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> + c<sup>2</sup> + 96 = 8(a + b – 2c), then √(ab – bc + ca) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For an equation of form a2 + b2 + c2 + Constant = 2(xa + yb + zc), the values are a = x, b = y, and c = z.

Rewrite given: a2 + b2 + c2 + 96 = 2(4a + 4b − 8c)

∴ a = 4, b = 4, and c = −8

Substitute in √(ab − bc + ca) ⇒ √((4 × 4) − (4 × −8) + (−8 × 4))

⇒ √(16 + 32 − 32) = √16 = 4

∴ The correct answer is 4.

Alternate Method

Given Equation: a2 + b2 + c2 + 96 = 8(a + b − 2c)

Method: Completing the square

⇒ a2 + b2 + c2 + 96 = 8a + 8b − 16c

⇒ (a2 − 8a) + (b2 − 8b) + (c2 + 16c) + 96 = 0

⇒ (a2 − 8a + 16) + (b2 − 8b + 16) + (c2 + 16c + 64) = 0

⇒ (a − 4)2 + (b − 4)2 + (c + 8)2 = 0

Since the sum of squares of real numbers is zero, each term must be zero:

⇒ a − 4 = 0 ⇒ a = 4

⇒ b − 4 = 0 ⇒ b = 4

⇒ c + 8 = 0 ⇒ c = −8

Now, evaluate √(ab − bc + ca):

⇒ √(4 × 4 − 4 × (−8) + (−8) × 4)

⇒ √(16 + 32 − 32) = √16 = 4

∴ The correct answer is 4.

Additional Information

Sum of Squares Property

If x2 + y2 + z2 = 0 for real numbers x, y, and z, then it must be that x = 0, y = 0, and z = 0.

Algebraic Identity

The square of a binomial is given by (x ± y)2 = x2 ± 2xy + y2. This is used to complete the square in algebraic equations.

Comparison Method

In expressions like a2 + b2 + c2 + k = 2(la + mb + nc), the values are directly found as a = l, b = m, and c = n if k = l2 + m2 + n2.

\(\left( {2\frac{6}{7} \text{ of } 4\frac{1}{5} \div \frac{2}{3}} \right) \times 1\frac{1}{9} \div \left( {\frac{3}{4} \times 2\frac{2}{3} \text{ of } \frac{1}{2} \div \frac{1}{4}} \right)\)

Formula used:

BODMAS rule

Calculation:

⇒ \(\left( {\frac{20}{7} \times \frac{21}{5} \div \frac{2}{3}} \right) \times \frac{10}{9} \div \left( {\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{8}{3} \times \frac{1}{2} \div \frac{1}{4}} \right)\)

questions.question: The value of \(\frac{{(\cos 9^\circ \; + \;\sin 81^\circ )\;\left( {sec9^\circ \; + \;cosec81^\circ } \right)}}{{\sin 56^\circ \sec 34^\circ \; + \;\cos 25^\circ cosec65^\circ }}\) is∶
questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\frac{{(\cos 9^\circ \; + \;\sin 81^\circ )\;\left( {sec9^\circ \; + \;cosec81^\circ } \right)}}{{\sin 56^\circ \sec 34^\circ \; + \;\cos 25^\circ cosec65^\circ }}\) is∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Convert terms using complementary angles: sin 81° = cos 9° and cosec 81° = sec 9°.

Numerator = (cos 9° + cos 9°) × (sec 9° + sec 9°) = 2 cos 9° × 2 sec 9° = 4(cos 9° × sec 9°) = 4.

Denominator = sin 56° sec 34° + cos 25° cosec 65° = 1 + 1 = 2 [since sin A sec(90°−A) = 1].

Value = 4 ÷ 2 = 2.

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Alternate Method

Given: expression = ((cos 9° + sin 81°)(sec 9° + cosec 81°)) ÷ (sin 56° sec 34° + cos 25° cosec 65°)

Formula Used: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ; cosec(90° − θ) = sec θ; cos θ × sec θ = 1; sin θ × cosec θ = 1

⇒ Numerator = (cos 9° + sin(90° − 9°)) × (sec 9° + cosec(90° − 9°))

⇒ Numerator = (cos 9° + cos 9°) × (sec 9° + sec 9°)

⇒ Numerator = 2 cos 9° × 2 sec 9° = 4(cos 9° × sec 9°) = 4 × 1 = 4

⇒ Denominator = sin 56° sec(90° − 56°) + cos 25° cosec(90° − 25°)

⇒ Denominator = (sin 56° × cosec 56°) + (cos 25° × sec 25°)

⇒ Denominator = 1 + 1 = 2

⇒ Expression Value = 4 ÷ 2 = 2

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Additional Information

Complementary Angle Identities

For any angle θ, sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

Reciprocal Identities

Product of reciprocal ratios is always 1: sin θ × cosec θ = 1, cos θ × sec θ = 1, and tan θ × cot θ = 1.

Special Product Rule

If A + B = 90°, then sin A sec B = 1 and cos A cosec B = 1 because sec B = cosec A and cosec B = sec A.

questions.question: A train travelling at the speed of x km/h crossed a 200 m long platform in 30 seconds and overtook a man walking in the same direction at the speed of 6 km/h in 20 seconds. What is the value of x?
questions.questionHtml: A train travelling at the speed of x km/h crossed a 200 m long platform in 30 seconds and overtook a man walking in the same direction at the speed of 6 km/h in 20 seconds. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Distance difference = Platform length = 200 m.

This difference arises from the difference in (Effective Speed × Time).

200 = [x × 30 − (x − 6) × 20] × 5/18

200 × 18/5 = 30x − 20x + 120

720 = 10x + 120 ⇒ 10x = 600 ⇒ x = 60

∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of train = x km/h

Length of platform = 200 m

Time to cross platform = 30 s

Speed of man = 6 km/h (same direction)

Time to overtake man = 20 s

Formula Used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative speed (same direction) = S1 − S2

Conversion: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

Calculations:

Let the length of the train be L meters.

For crossing the platform:

⇒ L + 200 = [x × 5/18] × 30

⇒ L + 200 = 25x/3 ... (Eq. 1)

For overtaking the man:

⇒ Relative Speed = (x − 6) × 5/18 m/s

⇒ L = [(x − 6) × 5/18] × 20

⇒ L = 50(x − 6)/9 ... (Eq. 2)

Substitute Eq. 2 into Eq. 1:

⇒ [50(x − 6)/9] + 200 = 25x/3

Multiply the entire equation by 9 to clear denominators:

⇒ 50(x − 6) + 1800 = 75x

⇒ 50x − 300 + 1800 = 75x

⇒ 1500 = 75x − 50x

⇒ 1500 = 25x

⇒ x = 1500 ÷ 25

⇒ x = 60

∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is S1 − S2. When they move in opposite directions, relative speed is S1 + S2.

Train Crossing Objects

To cross a point object (pole/man), distance = length of train. To cross a platform/bridge/tunnel, distance = length of train + length of object.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: If \(x = \sqrt {1 + \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{2}} - \sqrt {1 - \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{2}} \) then the value of \(\frac{{\sqrt 2 - x}}{{\sqrt 2 + x}}\) will be closest to∶
questions.questionHtml: If \(x = \sqrt {1 + \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{2}} - \sqrt {1 - \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{2}} \) then the value of \(\frac{{\sqrt 2 - x}}{{\sqrt 2 + x}}\) will be closest to∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Square x directly: x2 = (1 + √3/2) + (1 − √3/2) − 2√[(1 + √3/2)(1 − √3/2)]

x2 = 2 − 2√(1 − 3/4) = 2 − 2(1/2) = 1 ⇒ x = 1.

Required value = (√2 − 1) / (√2 + 1) = (1.414 − 1) / (1.414 + 1)

0.414 / 2.414 ≈ 0.17.

∴ The correct answer is 0.17.

Alternate Method

Given: x = √(1 + √3/2) − √(1 − √3/2)

Formula Used: (a − b)2 = a2 + b2 − 2ab

⇒ x = √[(2 + √3)/2] − √[(2 − √3)/2]

⇒ x = [√(4 + 2√3) / 2] − [√(4 − 2√3) / 2] (Multiplying √2 to numerator and denominator)

⇒ Since 4 + 2√3 = (√3 + 1)2 and 4 − 2√3 = (√3 − 1)2

⇒ x = [(√3 + 1) − (√3 − 1)] / 2 = 2 / 2 = 1

⇒ Required Expression = (√2 − 1) / (√2 + 1)

⇒ Rationalizing: [(√2 − 1) × (√2 − 1)] / [(√2 + 1) × (√2 − 1)]

⇒ (2 + 1 − 2√2) / (2 − 1) = 3 − 2√2

⇒ Value = 3 − 2(1.414) = 3 − 2.828 = 0.172

∴ The correct answer is 0.17.

Additional Information

Simplification of Nested Radicals

A radical of the form √(a ± 2√b) can be simplified to √m ± √n where m + n = a and m × n = b.

Rationalization of Denominator

To remove a surd from the denominator, multiply both numerator and denominator by the conjugate (e.g., conjugate of a+√b is a−√b).

Common Square Root Values

√2 ≈ 1.414, √3 ≈ 1.732, and √5 ≈ 2.236 are frequently used in competitive exams.

questions.question: If a 3 + b 3 = 218 and a + b = 2, then the value of ab is∶
questions.questionHtml: If a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup> = 218 and a + b = 2, then the value of ab is∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the expansion: a3 + b3 = (a + b)((a + b)2 − 3ab)

Substitute the given values: 218 = 2(22 − 3ab)

Divide both sides by 2: 109 = 4 − 3ab

Rearrange to find 3ab: 3ab = 4 − 109 = −105

Solve for ab: ab = −105 ÷ 3 = −35

∴ The correct answer is -35.

Alternate Method

Given: a3 + b3 = 218 and a + b = 2

Formula Used: (a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)

⇒ (2)3 = 218 + 3ab(2)

⇒ 8 = 218 + 6ab

⇒ 6ab = 8 − 218

⇒ 6ab = −210

⇒ ab = −210 ÷ 6

⇒ ab = −35

∴ The correct answer is -35.

Additional Information

Cube of Sum Formula

(a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b). This identity connects the sum of cubes to the sum and product of two numbers.

Sum of Cubes Identity

a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2). This is a factoring identity frequently used in simplification.

Algebraic Properties

For any two numbers, the relationship between their sum (S = a+b) and product (P = ab) for powers can be generalized as a3 + b3 = S3 − 3SP.

questions.question: What will be the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 31,250 for 2 years at 12% p.a, if the interest is compounded 8-month?
questions.questionHtml: What will be the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 31,250 for 2 years at 12% p.a, if the interest is compounded 8-month?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For 8-month compounding, Rate = 12% × (8/12) = 8% and Periods = (2 × 12) ÷ 8 = 3.

Using 3 : 3 : 1 ratio for 3 periods:

Level 1: 8% of 31250 = 2500 → 2500 × 3 = 7500

Level 2: 8% of 2500 = 200 → 200 × 3 = 600

Level 3: 8% of 200 = 16 → 16 × 1 = 16

Total Compound Interest = 7500 + 600 + 16 = 8116.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 8,116.

Alternate Method

Given: Principal (P) = Rs. 31,250 | Rate (R) = 12% p.a. | Time (T) = 2 years

Formula Used: A = P(1 + r/100)n ; CI = A − P

⇒ New Rate (r) = 12 × (8/12) = 8% per compounding period

⇒ Number of periods (n) = (2 × 12) ÷ 8 = 3 periods

⇒ Amount (A) = 31250 × (1 + 8/100)3

⇒ A = 31250 × (27/25)3

⇒ A = 31250 × (19683 / 15625)

⇒ A = 2 × 19683 = Rs. 39,366

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = A − P = 39366 − 31250 = Rs. 8,116

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 8,116.

Additional Information

Effective Rate of Interest

For two successive periods with rates x% and y%, the effective rate is [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 periods: Difference = P(r/100)2. For 3 periods: Difference = P(r/100)2 × (3 + r/100).

Compounding Frequencies

If interest is compounded k-monthly, new rate R′ = R × (k/12) and total periods n = (T in months) ÷ k.

questions.questionHtml: The value of the expression (cos<sup>6</sup>θ + sin<sup>6</sup>θ – 1) (tan<sup>2</sup>θ + cot<sup>2</sup>θ + 2) is∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the value substitution method: Let θ = 45°.

Value of (cos645° + sin645° − 1) = ((1/√2)6 + (1/√2)6 − 1) = (1/8 + 1/8 − 1) = −3/4.

Value of (tan245° + cot245° + 2) = (12 + 12 + 2) = 4.

Product = (−3/4) × 4 = −3.

∴ The correct answer is -3.

Alternate Method

Given: (cos6θ + sin6θ − 1) (tan2θ + cot2θ + 2)

Formula Used:

1. sin6θ + cos6θ = (sin2θ + cos2θ)3 − 3sin2θcos2θ(sin2θ + cos2θ) = 1 − 3sin2θcos2θ

2. tan2θ + cot2θ + 2 = (tanθ + cotθ)2 = (sinθ/cosθ + cosθ/sinθ)2 = (1 / sinθcosθ)2

⇒ Let Part 1 = (cos6θ + sin6θ − 1)

⇒ Part 1 = (1 − 3sin2θcos2θ − 1) = −3sin2θcos2θ

⇒ Let Part 2 = (tan2θ + cot2θ + 2) = (tanθ + cotθ)2

⇒ Part 2 = (sinθ/cosθ + cosθ/sinθ)2 = ((sin2θ + cos2θ) / sinθcosθ)2 = 1 / (sin2θcos2θ)

⇒ Expression = Part 1 × Part 2 = (−3sin2θcos2θ) × (1 / sin2θcos2θ)

⇒ Expression = −3

∴ The correct answer is -3.

Additional Information

Pythagorean Identities

Standard identities: sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, sec2θ − tan2θ = 1, and cosec2θ − cot2θ = 1.

Sum of Higher Powers

sin4θ + cos4θ = 1 − 2sin2θcos2θ and sin6θ + cos6θ = 1 − 3sin2θcos2θ.

Reciprocal Sum Property

tanθ + cotθ = 1 / (sinθ cosθ) = secθ cosecθ.

questions.question: When 12,16, 18, 20 and 25 divide the least number x, the remainder in each case is 4 but x is divisible by 7. What is the digit at the thousands’ place in x?
questions.questionHtml: When 12,16, 18, 20 and 25 divide the least number x, the remainder in each case is 4 but x is divisible by 7. What is the digit at the thousands’ place in x?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

LCM(12, 16, 18, 20, 25) = 3600.

General form of x = 3600k + 4.

To be divisible by 7, 3600k + 4 → 2k + 4 must be a multiple of 7 (since 3600 ÷ 7 leaves remainder 2).

Smallest k satisfying this is 5 (2 × 5 + 4 = 14).

Number x = 3600 × 5 + 4 = 18004.

Thousands' place digit in 18004 is 8.

∴ The correct answer is 8.

Alternate Method

Given: Divisors = 12, 16, 18, 20, 25; Remainder = 4; x is divisible by 7.

Formula: Number x = LCM(divisors) × k + Remainder

⇒ Prime factors of 12 = 22 × 3

⇒ Prime factors of 16 = 24

⇒ Prime factors of 18 = 2 × 32

⇒ Prime factors of 20 = 22 × 5

⇒ Prime factors of 25 = 52

⇒ LCM = 24 × 32 × 52 = 16 × 9 × 25 = 3600

⇒ Number x = 3600k + 4

⇒ To satisfy x ÷ 7, (3600k + 4) mod 7 = 0

⇒ (7 × 514 + 2)k + 4 ≡ 0 mod 7

⇒ 2k + 4 ≡ 0 mod 7

⇒ For k = 5, 2(5) + 4 = 14, which is divisible by 7

⇒ x = 3600 × 5 + 4 = 18000 + 4 = 18004

⇒ In 18004, the thousands' place digit is 8.

∴ The correct answer is 8.

Additional Information

LCM for remainders

When a number N leaves the same remainder r for different divisors, N = LCM(divisors) × k + r.

Modular Congruence

To find k, simplify the coefficient of k by dividing the LCM by the secondary divisor (in this case, 7) and checking the remainder.

Place Value Chart

Starting from right: Units, Tens, Hundreds, Thousands, Ten-thousands, etc. The digit 8 in 18,004 is in the fourth position from the right.

questions.question: In ΔABC, D and E are the points on sides AB and BC respectively such that DE∥ AC. If AD ∶ DB = 5 ∶ 3, then what is the ratio of the area of ΔBDE to that of the trapezium ACED?
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, D and E are the points on sides AB and BC respectively such that DE∥ AC. If AD ∶ DB = 5 ∶ 3, then what is the ratio of the area of ΔBDE to that of the trapezium ACED?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of sides DB : AB = 3 : (3 + 5) = 3 : 8.

Area ratio of similar triangles is square of side ratio: Area(ΔBDE) : Area(ΔBAC) = 32 : 82 = 9 : 64.

Area of trapezium ACED = Area(ΔBAC) − Area(ΔBDE) = 64 − 9 = 55.

Required ratio Area(ΔBDE) : Area(Trapezium ACED) = 9 : 55.

∴ The correct answer is 9 ∶ 55.

Alternate Method

Given: DE ∥ AC and AD ∶ DB = 5 ∶ 3.

Formula Used: Ratio of areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

 

⇒ Let DB = 3x and AD = 5x.

⇒ Total side AB = AD + DB = 5x + 3x = 8x.

⇒ In ΔBDE and ΔBAC, ∠B is common and ∠BDE = ∠BAC (corresponding angles as DE ∥ AC).

⇒ By AA similarity, ΔBDE ≈ ΔBAC.

⇒ Area(ΔBDE) / Area(ΔBAC) = (DB / AB)2

⇒ Area(ΔBDE) / Area(ΔBAC) = (3x / 8x)2 = 9 / 64.

⇒ Let Area(ΔBDE) = 9 units and Area(ΔBAC) = 64 units.

⇒ Area(Trapezium ACED) = Area(ΔBAC) − Area(ΔBDE)

⇒ Area(Trapezium ACED) = 64 − 9 = 55 units.

⇒ Required Ratio = Area(ΔBDE) ∶ Area(Trapezium ACED) = 9 ∶ 55.

∴ The correct answer is 9 ∶ 55.

Additional Information

Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem)

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio: BD/DA = BE/EC.

Area Property of Similar Triangles

If ΔABC ≈ ΔPQR, then Area(ΔABC)/Area(ΔPQR) = (AB/PQ)2 = (BC/QR)2 = (AC/PR)2.

Area of Trapezium

Area = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × (Distance between them). In similarity problems, it is usually found by subtracting the smaller triangle from the larger one.

questions.question: In ΔABC, D is a point on side BC such that ∠ADC = ∠BAC. If CA = 12 cm, CD = 8 cm, then CB is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, D is a point on side BC such that ∠ADC = ∠BAC. If CA = 12 cm, CD = 8 cm, then CB is equal to∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When ∠ADC = ∠BAC in ΔABC, the relation between sides is CA2 = CB × CD.

Given: CA = 12 cm and CD = 8 cm.

⇒ 122 = CB × 8

⇒ 144 = 8 × CB

⇒ CB = 144 ÷ 8 = 18 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

CA = 12 cm

CD = 8 cm

∠ADC = ∠BAC

In ΔABC and ΔDAC:

⇒ ∠C = ∠C (Common angle)

⇒ ∠BAC = ∠ADC (Given)

⇒ ΔABC ∼ ΔDAC (By AA similarity criterion)

Since the triangles are similar, the ratios of their corresponding sides are equal:

⇒ BC / AC = AC / CD

⇒ BC / 12 = 12 / 8

⇒ BC × 8 = 12 × 12

⇒ 8 × BC = 144

⇒ BC = 144 ÷ 8

⇒ BC = 18 cm

∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.

Additional Information

AA Similarity Criterion

If two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another triangle, then the two triangles are similar.

Ratio of Areas of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(Δ1) ÷ Area(Δ2) = (s1 ÷ s2)2.

Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem)

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle intersecting the other two sides, then it divides the two sides in the same ratio.

questions.question: In ΔABC, ∠A = 52° and O is the orthocentre of the triangle (BO and CO meet AC and AB at E and F respectively when produced). If the bisectors of ∠OBC and ∠OCB meet at P, then the measure of ∠ BPC is∶
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, ∠A = 52° and O is the orthocentre of the triangle (BO and CO meet AC and AB at E and F respectively when produced). If the bisectors of ∠OBC and ∠OCB meet at P, then the measure of ∠ BPC is∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Direct formula for the angle at point P where bisectors of angles formed by orthocentre meet:

∠BPC = 180° − (∠A ÷ 2)

Given ∠A = 52°

⇒ ∠BPC = 180° − (52° ÷ 2) = 180° − 26° = 154°.

∴ The correct answer is 154°.

Alternate Method

Given: ∠A = 52°, O is the orthocentre, P is the intersection of bisectors of ∠OBC and ∠OCB.

Formula Used:

1. In ΔABC, if O is orthocentre: ∠BOC = 180° − ∠A

2. In ΔOBC, if P is incenter (intersection of bisectors): ∠BPC = 90° + (∠BOC ÷ 2)

Calculations:

⇒ In ΔABC, ∠BOC = 180° − ∠A

⇒ ∠BOC = 180° − 52° = 128°

⇒ Now, in ΔOBC, BP and CP are the bisectors of ∠OBC and ∠OCB respectively.

⇒ ∴ P is the incenter of ΔOBC.

⇒ ∠BPC = 90° + (∠BOC ÷ 2)

⇒ ∠BPC = 90° + (128° ÷ 2)

⇒ ∠BPC = 90° + 64°

⇒ ∠BPC = 154°

∴ The correct answer is 154°.

Additional Information

Orthocentre Property

The angle subtended by any side at the orthocentre (O) is supplementary to the opposite angle of the triangle: ∠BOC + ∠A = 180°.

Incenter Angle Property

The angle formed at the incenter (intersection of internal angle bisectors) is given by 90° + (opposite angle ÷ 2).

Circumcentre Angle Property

The angle subtended by any side at the circumcentre is twice the angle subtended at the remaining part of the circle: ∠BOC = 2 × ∠A.

Ex-center Angle Property

The angle formed at the ex-center (intersection of two external bisectors) is 90° − (opposite angle ÷ 2).

questions.question: If a cuboid of dimensions 32 cm × 12 cm × 9 cm is melted and recast into two equal cubes of the same size, what will be the ratio of the total surface area of the cuboid to the total surface area of the two cubes?
questions.questionHtml: If a cuboid of dimensions 32 cm × 12 cm × 9 cm is melted and recast into two equal cubes of the same size, what will be the ratio of the total surface area of the cuboid to the total surface area of the two cubes?

As we know

Volume of cuboid = lbh

Total surface of area of cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)

Volume of cube = a3

questions.question: A certain number of persons can complete a work in 34 days working 9 h a day. If the number of persons is decreased by 40% then how many hours a day should the remaining persons work to complete the work in 51 days?
questions.questionHtml: A certain number of persons can complete a work in 34 days working 9 h a day. If the number of persons is decreased by 40% then how many hours a day should the remaining persons work to complete the work in 51 days?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of persons = 100 : 60 = 5 : 3

Apply M1D1H1 = M2D2H2

5 × 34 × 9 = 3 × 51 × H2

1530 = 153 × H2

H2 = 10

∴ The correct answer is 10 hours.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial days (D1) = 34 days, Initial hours (H1) = 9 h

Initial persons (M1) = x (Let it be 100 units)

New days (D2) = 51 days, New persons (M2) = 60 units (40% decrease)

Formula Used:

M1 × D1 × H1 = M2 × D2 × H2

⇒ 100 × 34 × 9 = 60 × 51 × H2

⇒ 30600 = 3060 × H2

⇒ H2 = 30600 ÷ 3060

⇒ H2 = 10 hours

∴ The correct answer is 10 hours.

Additional Information

Chain Rule Formula

(M1 × D1 × H1 × E1) ÷ W1 = (M2 × D2 × H2 × E2) ÷ W2 where E is efficiency and W is work.

Inverse Proportion

For a constant amount of work, the number of persons is inversely proportional to the time taken (Days × Hours).

Unitary Method for Work

If 1 person does work in D days, total work is D person-days. For H hours per day, it is D × H person-hours.

questions.question: In a trapezium ABCD, DC ∥ AB, AB = 12 cm and DC = 7.2cm. What is the length of the line segment joining the mid-points of its diagonals?
questions.questionHtml: In a trapezium ABCD, DC ∥ AB, AB = 12 cm and DC = 7.2cm. What is the length of the line segment joining the mid-points of its diagonals?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For any trapezium with parallel sides a and b, the length of the line segment joining the mid-points of its diagonals is given by the formula:

Length = |a − b| ÷ 2

Here, a = 12 cm and b = 7.2 cm.

Length = (12 − 7.2) ÷ 2 = 4.8 ÷ 2 = 2.4 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 2.4 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Parallel side AB = 12 cm

Parallel side DC = 7.2 cm

Line segment PQ joins the mid-points of diagonals AC and BD.

Formula Used:

Length of the line segment joining mid-points of diagonals = (Difference of parallel sides) ÷ 2

Calculations:

⇒ Let P be the mid-point of AC and Q be the mid-point of BD.

⇒ PQ = (AB − DC) ÷ 2

⇒ PQ = (12 − 7.2) ÷ 2

⇒ PQ = 4.8 ÷ 2

⇒ PQ = 2.4 cm

∴ The correct answer is 2.4 cm.

Additional Information

Median of a Trapezium

The line segment joining the mid-points of the non-parallel sides is called the median. Its length is the average of the parallel sides: Median = (a + b) ÷ 2.

Area of a Trapezium

The area is calculated as Area = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height = 1/2 × (a + b) × h.

Property of Diagonals

In any trapezium, the sum of the squares of the diagonals is equal to the sum of the squares of the non-parallel sides plus twice the product of the parallel sides: AC2 + BD2 = AD2 + BC2 + 2(AB × CD).

questions.question: If 40% of the number of employees in office A are shifted equally to office B and E, then what is the difference between the number of employees in B and that in C?
questions.questionHtml: If 40% of the number of employees in office A are shifted equally to office B and E, then what is the difference between the number of employees in B and that in C?
questions.solution:
Total number of employees in all offices = 2400

Number of employees in office B = 2400 × (18/360) = 120

Number of employees in office A = 2400 × (126/360) = 840

40% of the number of employees in office A = 840 × (40/100) = 336

Number of employees who shifted to office B = 336/2 = 168

Number of employees in office B after sifting = 168 + 120 = 288

Number of employees in office C = 2400 × (54/360) = 360

Required difference between the number of employees in B and that in C = 360 – 288 = 72

questions.question: The sides AB and AC of ΔABC are produced to P and Q respectively. The bisectors of ∠CBP and ∠BCQ meet at R. If the measure of ∠A = 44°, the find the measure of ∠BRC/2.
questions.questionHtml: The sides AB and AC of ΔABC are produced to P and Q respectively. The bisectors of ∠CBP and ∠BCQ meet at R. If the measure of ∠A = 44°, the find the measure of ∠BRC/2.

∴ The correct answer is 34°.

Given:

Measure of ∠A = 44°

Point R is the intersection of external bisectors of ∠B and ∠C.

Formula Used:

For ΔABC, if external bisectors of ∠B and ∠C meet at R, then ∠BRC = 90° − ∠A ÷ 2.

Calculations:

⇒ ∠BRC = 90° − (44° ÷ 2)

⇒ ∠BRC = 90° − 22°

⇒ ∠BRC = 68°

⇒ Required measurement = ∠BRC ÷ 2

⇒ Required measurement = 68° ÷ 2 = 34°

∴ The correct answer is 34°.

Additional Information

Incenter Angle Property

The angle formed by the intersection of internal angle bisectors is ∠BIC = 90° + ∠A ÷ 2.

Excenter Definition

An excenter is the point where the bisector of one interior angle and the bisectors of the two opposite exterior angles intersect.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of a triangle is always 180°, while the sum of exterior angles (one at each vertex) is 360°.

questions.question: If a nine-digit number 389x6378y is divisible by 72, then the value of √(6x + 7y) will be∶
questions.questionHtml: If a nine-digit number 389x6378y is divisible by 72, then the value of √(6x + 7y) will be∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For divisibility by 72, the number must be divisible by 8 and 9.

Check 8: Last three digits 78y must be divisible by 8 → 784 ÷ 8 = 98 ∴ y = 4.

Check 9: Sum of digits (3+8+9+x+6+3+7+8+4) = 48 + x must be divisible by 9 ∴ x = 6.

Substitute: √(6 × 6 + 7 × 4) = √(36 + 28) = √64 = 8.

∴ The correct answer is 8.

Alternate Method

Given: Nine-digit number 389x6378y is divisible by 72.

Formula Used: Divisibility by 72 ⇒ Divisibility by 8 AND Divisibility by 9.

Step 1: Divisibility rule for 8 (Last 3 digits 78y must be divisible by 8).

⇒ 78y ÷ 8

⇒ 784 ÷ 8 = 98 (Perfectly divisible)

⇒ y = 4

Step 2: Divisibility rule for 9 (Sum of all digits must be divisible by 9).

⇒ Sum = 3 + 8 + 9 + x + 6 + 3 + 7 + 8 + 4

⇒ Sum = 48 + x

⇒ The next multiple of 9 after 48 is 54.

⇒ 48 + x = 54

⇒ x = 54 − 48 = 6

Step 3: Calculate the required value √(6x + 7y).

⇒ √(6 × 6 + 7 × 4)

⇒ √(36 + 28)

⇒ √64

⇒ 8

∴ The correct answer is 8.

Additional Information

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8 or are all zeros.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its individual digits is a multiple of 9.

Composite Divisibility

To check divisibility by a composite number (like 72), check for divisibility by its coprime factors (8 and 9 in this case).

questions.question: If 2√2x 3 – 3√3y 3 = (√2 x – √3 y) (Ax 2 + By 2 + Cxy), then the value of A 2 + B 2 – C 2 is∶
questions.questionHtml: If 2√2x3 – 3√3y3 = (√2 x – √3 y) (Ax2 + By2 + Cxy), then the value of A2 + B2 – C2 is∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify a and b from the identity a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + b2 + ab).

Here, a = √2x and b = √3y.

Comparing the RHS, we get A = a2 = 2, B = b2 = 3, and C = ab = √6.

Calculate A2 + B2 − C2 = 22 + 32 − (√6)2.

Value = 4 + 9 − 6 = 7.

∴ The correct answer is 7.

Alternate Method

Given:

2√2x3 − 3√3y3 = (√2x − √3y)(Ax2 + By2 + Cxy)

Formula Used:

a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + b2 + ab)

Calculations:

⇒ 2√2x3 − 3√3y3 can be written as (√2x)3 − (√3y)3.

⇒ Applying the formula: (√2x − √3y)[(√2x)2 + (√3y)2 + (√2x)(√3y)]

⇒ (√2x − √3y)(2x2 + 3y2 + √6xy)

⇒ Comparing with the given expression (Ax2 + By2 + Cxy):

⇒ A = 2, B = 3, C = √6

⇒ Required value = A2 + B2 − C2

⇒ (2)2 + (3)2 − (√6)2

⇒ 4 + 9 − 6 = 7

∴ The correct answer is 7.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identities for Cubes

The sum of cubes is given by a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 + b2 − ab). Note the sign change in the last term.

Comparison of Coefficients

When two polynomial expressions are equal for all values of variables, the coefficients of like powers and like terms (like x2, y2, xy) must be equal.

Squaring Irrationals

The square of a square root of a number is the number itself: (√n)2 = n. For example, (√6)2 = 6.

questions.question: If \(\sqrt {86 - 60\sqrt 2 } \; = \;a - b\sqrt 2 ,\) then what will be the value of √(a 2 + b 2 ), correct to one decimal place?
questions.questionHtml: If \(\sqrt {86 - 60\sqrt 2 } \; = \;a - b\sqrt 2 ,\) then what will be the value of √(a2 + b2), correct to one decimal place?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Rewrite the expression in the form √(X − 2√Y) to identify factors.

√(86 − 2 × 30√2) ⇒ Factors of 30√2 whose squares sum to 86 are 6 and 5√2.

Since 62 + (5√2)2 = 36 + 50 = 86, the root is |5√2 − 6|.

Comparing 5√2 − 6 with a − b√2 ⇒ a = −6 and b = −5.

√(a2 + b2) = √((−6)2 + (−5)2) = √(36 + 25) = √61 ≈ 7.8.

∴ The correct answer is 7.8.

Alternate Method

Given: √(86 − 60√2) = a − b√2

Squaring both sides:

⇒ 86 − 60√2 = (a − b√2)2

⇒ 86 − 60√2 = a2 + (b√2)2 − 2 × a × b√2

⇒ 86 − 60√2 = (a2 + 2b2) − (2ab)√2

By comparing the rational and irrational parts:

⇒ 2ab = 60 ⇒ ab = 30

⇒ a2 + 2b2 = 86

Testing factors of 30: If a = −6 and b = −5 (to ensure a − b√2 is positive):

⇒ (−6)2 + 2(−5)2 = 36 + 2(25) = 36 + 50 = 86 (Condition satisfied)

Now, find √(a2 + b2):

⇒ √((−6)2 + (−5)2) = √(36 + 25) = √61

⇒ Since 7.82 = 60.84 and 7.92 = 62.41

⇒ √61 ≈ 7.8 (to one decimal place)

∴ The correct answer is 7.8.

Additional Information

Square Root of Nested Surds

To solve √(x ± √y), we express the term inside as a perfect square (u ± v)2 = u2 + v2 ± 2uv, where u2 + v2 = x and 2uv = √y.

Linear Approximation of Square Roots

For a number n near a perfect square s2, √n ≈ s + (n − s2) / (2s). For example, √61 ≈ 8 + (61 − 64) / 16 = 8 − 0.1875 = 7.8125.

Properties of Square Roots

The principal square root √x is always non-negative. Therefore, if √X = a − b√2, then the value of a − b√2 must be ≥ 0.

questions.questionHtml: To do a certain work, the ration of efficiency of A to that of B is 3 ∶ 7 Working together, they can complete the work in \(10\frac{1}{2}\) days. They work together for 8 days. 60% of the remaining work will be completed by A alone in∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total efficiency of A and B = 3 + 7 = 10 units/day.

Remaining time for both to finish the work = 10.5 − 8 = 2.5 days.

Remaining work units = 10 × 2.5 = 25 units.

Required work (60% of remaining) = 0.60 × 25 = 15 units.

Time taken by A alone = 15 ÷ 3 = 5 days.

∴ The correct answer is 5 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Efficiency ratio A : B = 3 : 7

Time taken together = 10.5 days (or 21/2 days)

Time worked together = 8 days

Person Total Days Total Work Efficiency
A 35 days 105 units 3
B 15 days 7

⇒ Total efficiency of A + B = 3 + 7 = 10 units/day.

⇒ Total work = Combined efficiency × Total days = 10 × 10.5 = 105 units.

⇒ Work done in 8 days = 10 × 8 = 80 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 105 − 80 = 25 units.

⇒ 60% of remaining work = 25 × (60 ÷ 100) = 15 units.

⇒ Time taken by A = Work ÷ Efficiency of A = 15 ÷ 3 = 5 days.

∴ The correct answer is 5 days.

Additional Information

Fundamental Work Equation

The relationship between work, efficiency, and time is given by Work = Efficiency × Time.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a constant amount of work (E ∝ 1/T).

Combined Efficiency

When multiple people work together, their combined efficiency is the sum of their individual efficiencies (ETotal = E1 + E2 + ... + En).

questions.question: Abhi rows upstream a distance of 28 km in 4 h and rows downstream a distance of 50 km in 2 h to row a distance of 44.8 km in still water, he will take∶
questions.questionHtml: Abhi rows upstream a distance of 28 km in 4 h and rows downstream a distance of 50 km in 2 h to row a distance of 44.8 km in still water, he will take∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Upstream Speed = 28 ÷ 4 = 7 kmph

Downstream Speed = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 kmph

Speed of boat in still water = (Upstream + Downstream) ÷ 2 = (7 + 25) ÷ 2 = 16 kmph

Required time = 44.8 ÷ 16 = 2.8 h

∴ The correct answer is 2.8 h.

Alternate Method

Given: Upstream distance = 28 km in 4 h, Downstream distance = 50 km in 2 h.

Formula Used: Speed = Distance ÷ Time; Speed in Still Water (v) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

⇒ Upstream speed (u) = 28 ÷ 4 = 7 kmph

⇒ Downstream speed (d) = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 kmph

⇒ Speed of boat in still water (v) = (d + u) ÷ 2

⇒ v = (25 + 7) ÷ 2 = 32 ÷ 2 = 16 kmph

⇒ Time taken to cover 44.8 km in still water = Distance ÷ v

⇒ Time = 44.8 ÷ 16 = 2.8 h

∴ The correct answer is 2.8 h.

Additional Information

Speed of Boat in Still Water (v)

The speed of the boat when the water is stationary. v = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream (s)

The rate at which the river water flows. s = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Downstream and Upstream Speed

Downstream Speed = v + s; Upstream Speed = v − s.

questions.question: The graph of the equation x – 7y = -42 intersects the y-axis at P(α, β) and the graph of 6x + y – 15 = 0, intersects the x-axis at Q(γ, δ) what is the value of α + β + γ + δ?
questions.questionHtml: The graph of the equation x – 7y = -42 intersects the y-axis at P(α, β) and the graph of 6x + y – 15 = 0, intersects the x-axis at Q(γ, δ) what is the value of α + β + γ + δ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

To find y-axis intersection (P), set x = 0: 0 − 7y = −42 ⇒ y = 6. Thus, α = 0, β = 6.

To find x-axis intersection (Q), set y = 0: 6x + 0 − 15 = 0 ⇒ 6x = 15 ⇒ x = 2.5. Thus, γ = 2.5, δ = 0.

Required sum: α + β + γ + δ = 0 + 6 + 2.5 + 0 = 8.5.

In fraction form: 8.5 = 17/2.

∴ The correct answer is 17/2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Equation 1: x − 7y = −42

Equation 2: 6x + y − 15 = 0

Points: P(α, β) on y-axis and Q(γ, δ) on x-axis.

Formula Used:

For intersection with y-axis, set x = 0.

For intersection with x-axis, set y = 0.

Calculations:

Step 1: Find coordinates of P(α, β)

⇒ At y-axis intersection, x = 0 ∴ α = 0.

⇒ 0 − 7y = −42

⇒ −7y = −42 ⇒ y = 6.

⇒ β = 6. Point P = (0, 6).

Step 2: Find coordinates of Q(γ, δ)

⇒ At x-axis intersection, y = 0 ∴ δ = 0.

⇒ 6x + 0 − 15 = 0

⇒ 6x = 15 ⇒ x = 15/6 = 2.5.

⇒ γ = 2.5. Point Q = (2.5, 0).

Step 3: Calculate the required sum

⇒ Sum = α + β + γ + δ

⇒ Sum = 0 + 6 + 2.5 + 0 = 8.5.

⇒ Sum = 17/2.

∴ The correct answer is 17/2.

Additional Information

X and Y Intercepts

The x-intercept is where a graph crosses the x-axis (y=0), and the y-intercept is where it crosses the y-axis (x=0).

Intercept Form of a Line

A line can be written as x/a + y/b = 1, where 'a' is the x-intercept and 'b' is the y-intercept.

General Linear Equation

For Ax + By + C = 0, the x-intercept is −C/A and the y-intercept is −C/B.

questions.question: If (a + b) ∶ (b + c) ∶ (c + a) = 7 ∶ 6 ∶ 5 and a + b + c = 27, then what will be the value of 1/a ∶ 1/b ∶ 1/c?
questions.questionHtml: If (a + b) ∶ (b + c) ∶ (c + a) = 7 ∶ 6 ∶ 5 and a + b + c = 27, then what will be the value of 1/a ∶ 1/b ∶ 1/c?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total units for 2(a + b + c) = 7 + 6 + 5 = 18 units.

Sum (a + b + c) = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 units.

Individual units: a = 9 − 6 = 3; b = 9 − 5 = 4; c = 9 − 7 = 2.

Required inverse ratio = 1/3 : 1/4 : 1/2.

Multiply by LCM(3, 4, 2) = 12 ⇒ 4 : 3 : 6.

∴ The correct answer is 4 : 3 : 6.

Alternate Method

Given:

(a + b) : (b + c) : (c + a) = 7 : 6 : 5

a + b + c = 27

Calculations:

⇒ Let a + b = 7k, b + c = 6k, and c + a = 5k.

⇒ Adding all: (a + b) + (b + c) + (c + a) = 7k + 6k + 5k

⇒ 2(a + b + c) = 18k ⇒ a + b + c = 9k

⇒ From the problem, a + b + c = 27, so 9k = 27 ⇒ k = 3

⇒ a = (a + b + c) − (b + c) = 27 − 6(3) = 27 − 18 = 9

⇒ b = (a + b + c) − (c + a) = 27 − 5(3) = 27 − 15 = 12

⇒ c = (a + b + c) − (a + b) = 27 − 7(3) = 27 − 21 = 6

⇒ 1/a : 1/b : 1/c = 1/9 : 1/12 : 1/6

⇒ Multiply by LCM(9, 12, 6) = 36: (36 ÷ 9) : (36 ÷ 12) : (36 ÷ 6) = 4 : 3 : 6

∴ The correct answer is 4 : 3 : 6.

Additional Information

Inverse Ratio

The inverse ratio of a : b : c is given by 1/a : 1/b : 1/c. To simplify, multiply by the LCM of the denominators.

Cyclic Ratio Property

For cyclic sums like (a+b), (b+c), and (c+a), the sum of the variables is always half the sum of the ratio parts.

Ratio and Constant of Proportionality

When values are given in ratio a : b : c, we can assume them to be ak, bk, and ck where k is the common multiplier.

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 11 cm, 60 and 61 cm. What is the radius of the circle circumscribing the triangle?
questions.questionHtml: The sides of a triangle are 11 cm, 60 and 61 cm. What is the radius of the circle circumscribing the triangle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify if the sides form a Pythagorean triple: 112 + 602 = 121 + 3600 = 3721 = 612.

Since it is a right-angled triangle, the circumcircle passes through all vertices and the hypotenuse acts as the diameter.

Circumradius (R) = Hypotenuse ÷ 2

R = 61 ÷ 2 = 30.5 cm

∴ The correct answer is 30.5 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Sides of the triangle = 11 cm, 60 cm, 61 cm

Formula Used:

For a right-angled triangle,

Radius of circumcircle (R) = Hypotenuse/2

Calculation:

Check whether the triangle is right-angled:

⇒ 112 + 602

⇒ 121 + 3600

⇒ 3721

⇒ 612 = 3721

Since 112 + 602 = 612, the triangle is right-angled.

Therefore, hypotenuse = 61 cm

⇒ R = 61/2 cm

⇒ R = 30.5 cm

∴ The radius of the circumscribed circle is 30.5 cm.

Additional Information

Inradius of Right Triangle

For a right-angled triangle, the inradius (r) is calculated as r = (Perpendicular + Base − Hypotenuse) ÷ 2.

Circumradius of Any Triangle

For any triangle with sides a, b, c and area Δ, the circumradius R = (abc) ÷ (4Δ).

Location of Circumcenter

In a right-angled triangle, the circumcenter lies exactly at the midpoint of the hypotenuse.

questions.question: One year ago, the ratio of the age (in years) of A to that of b was of 4 : 3 the ratio of their respective ages, 3 years from now, will be 6 ∶ 5. What will be the ratio of respective ages of A and B, 9 years from now?
questions.questionHtml: One year ago, the ratio of the age (in years) of A to that of b was of 4 : 3 the ratio of their respective ages, 3 years from now, will be 6 ∶ 5. What will be the ratio of respective ages of A and B, 9 years from now?
questions.solution:
Detailed Solution ∶

Let three years from now, the age ratio of A to B = 6x ∶ 5x

According to the question

⇒ (6x – 4)/(5x – 4) = 4/3

⇒ 3(6x – 4) = 4(5x – 4)

⇒ 18x – 12 = 20x – 16

⇒ 20x – 18x = 16 – 12

⇒ 2x = 4

⇒ x = 2

Three years from now, age of A = 6x = 6 × 2 = 12 years

9 years from now age of A = 12 + 6 = 18

Three years from now, age of B = 5x = 5 × 2 = 10 years

9 years from now, age of B = 10 + 6 = 16

Ratio of respective ages of A and B, 9 years from now = 18 ∶ 16 = 9 ∶ 8

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 120 quintals of wheat. 20% of it was sold at 25% loss. At what percent gain should he sell the rest to gain 25% on the whole transaction?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper bought 120 quintals of wheat. 20% of it was sold at 25% loss. At what percent gain should he sell the rest to gain 25% on the whole transaction?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of quantities = 20% : 80% = 1 : 4 (Total = 5 parts)

Net gain required on 5 parts = 5 × 25% = 125%

Actual gain/loss on 1 part = 1 × (−25%) = −25%

Balance gain required on 4 parts = 125% − (−25%) = 150%

Required gain % on rest = 150% ÷ 4 = 37.5% = 37½%

∴ The correct answer is 37½%.

Alternate Method

Given: Total wheat = 120 quintals | Part 1 = 20% at 25% loss | Target overall gain = 25%

Assume CP of 120 quintals = ₹12000 (at ₹100/quintal)

⇒ Total Target SP = 12000 × (125/100) = ₹15000

⇒ CP of 20% wheat (24 quintals) = ₹2400

⇒ SP of 20% wheat = 2400 × (75/100) = ₹1800

⇒ Remaining SP required = 15000 − 1800 = ₹13200

⇒ CP of remaining wheat (96 quintals) = ₹9600

⇒ Gain required on rest = 13200 − 9600 = ₹3600

⇒ Required Gain % = (3600 ÷ 9600) × 100

⇒ Required Gain % = 37.5% = 37½%

∴ The correct answer is 37½%.

Additional Information

Weighted Average Profit/Loss Formula

Overall Gain/Loss % = (n1p1 + n2p2) ÷ (n1 + n2), where n is quantity and p is profit/loss percentage (take loss as negative).

Successive Profit/Loss

When there are successive changes of a% and b%, the net change is [a + b + (a×b)/100] %.

Markup and Discount Relation

Profit % = Markup % − Discount % − (Markup × Discount) ÷ 100.

questions.question: Travelling at 60 km/h, a person reaches his destination at a certain time. He covers 60% of his journey in 2/5 th of the time. At what speed (in km/h) should he travel to cover the remaining journey so that he reaches the destination right on time?
questions.questionHtml: Travelling at 60 km/h, a person reaches his destination at a certain time. He covers 60% of his journey in 2/5<sup>th</sup> of the time. At what speed (in km/h) should he travel to cover the remaining journey so that he reaches the destination right on time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 40
Key Points
  • To solve this problem, we establish the relationship between Distance, Speed, and Time using the formula: Distance = Speed × Time.
  • Let the total Distance be D and the total Time scheduled for the journey be T. Since the person initially travels at 60 km/h to reach on time, we have:
    D = 60 × T
  • The journey is divided into two parts. In the First Part:
    Distance covered = 60% of D = 0.6D
    Time taken = 2/5th of T = 0.4T
  • In the Second Part (Remaining journey), we calculate the remaining values:
    Remaining Distance = D − 0.6D = 0.4D
    Remaining Time = T − 0.4T = 0.6T
  • The Required Speed (Vr) to cover the Remaining Distance in the Remaining Time is:
    Vr = (Remaining Distance) ÷ (Remaining Time)
    Vr = 0.4D ÷ 0.6T
  • Substitute the value of D (which is 60T) into the equation:
    Vr = (0.4 × 60T) ÷ 0.6T
    Vr = 24T ÷ 0.6T
    Vr = 24 ÷ 0.6 = 40 km/h
  • The logic shows that since the person covered a larger portion of the distance (60%) in a smaller portion of the time (40%), he can afford to slow down for the remainder of the trip. The correct speed is 40 km/h.
Additional Information
  • Average Speed: The average speed for the whole journey is the Total Distance divided by the Total Time. In this specific scenario, the average speed remains 60 km/h.
  • Ratio Method: You can also solve this by assuming values. Let T = 5 hours. Then D = 60 × 5 = 300 km.
    60% distance = 180 km covered in 2/5 of 5 hours = 2 hours.
    Remaining distance = 120 km to be covered in remaining 3 hours.
    Speed = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 km/h.
  • Inverse Proportion: When the distance is constant, Speed is inversely proportional to Time. When time is constant, Speed is directly proportional to Distance.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 5,000 is divided into two parts such that the simple interest on the first part for \(4\frac{1}{5}\) years at \(6\frac{2}{3}\% \;\) p.a is double the simple interest on the second part for \(2\frac{3}{4}\) years at 4% p.a. What is the difference between the two parts?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 5,000 is divided into two parts such that the simple interest on the first part for \(4\frac{1}{5}\) years at \(6\frac{2}{3}\% \;\)p.a is double the simple interest on the second part for \(2\frac{3}{4}\) years at 4% p.a. What is the difference between the two parts?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net Rate1 = 20/3 × 21/5 = 28% and Net Rate2 = 4 × 11/4 = 11%.

Given SI1 = 2 × SI2 ⇒ P1 × 28% = 2 × (P2 × 11%).

P1 × 28 = P2 × 22 ⇒ P1 : P2 = 11 : 14.

Total units = 11 + 14 = 25 units = ₹5,000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹200.

Difference between parts = |14 − 11| = 3 units = 3 × ₹200 = ₹600.

∴ The correct answer is ₹600.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Sum = ₹5,000

Part 1: T1 = 21/5 years, R1 = 20/3% p.a.

Part 2: T2 = 11/4 years, R2 = 4% p.a.

Condition: SI on first part = 2 × SI on second part

Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ Let the two parts be P1 and P2.

⇒ P1 + P2 = 5000 --- (i)

⇒ SI1 = (P1 × 20/3 × 21/5) ÷ 100 = (P1 × 4 × 7) ÷ 100 = 28P1/100

⇒ SI2 = (P2 × 4 × 11/4) ÷ 100 = 11P2/100

⇒ According to the question, SI1 = 2 × SI2

⇒ 28P1/100 = 2 × (11P2/100)

⇒ 28P1 = 22P2

⇒ P1/P2 = 22/28 = 11/14

⇒ P1 = (11/25) × 5000 = ₹2,200

⇒ P2 = (14/25) × 5000 = ₹2,800

⇒ Difference = P2 − P1 = 2800 − 2200 = ₹600.

∴ The correct answer is ₹600.

Additional Information

Simple Interest on Parts

If a sum P is divided into parts such that interests are equal, then P1:P2 = (1/R1T1) : (1/R2T2).

Amount in Simple Interest

Total Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI) = P × (1 + RT/100).

Successive Interest vs Simple Interest

Simple Interest is calculated on the original principal every year, whereas Compound Interest is calculated on the accumulated amount.

questions.question: What is the value of cosec(65° + θ) – sec(25° – θ) + tan 2 20° – cosec 2 70°?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of cosec(65° + θ) – sec(25° – θ) + tan<sup>2</sup>20° – cosec<sup>2</sup> 70°?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify complementary angles: (65° + θ) + (25° − θ) = 90°. Thus, csc(65° + θ) = sec(25° − θ), making their difference 0.

For the second part: 20° + 70° = 90°. Thus, csc 70° = sec 20°.

Substitute these into the expression: 0 + tan2 20° − sec2 20°.

Using the identity sec2 A − tan2 A = 1, we get tan2 A − sec2 A = −1.

Total value = 0 + (−1) = −1.

∴ The correct answer is -1.

Alternate Method

Given: csc(65° + θ) − sec(25° − θ) + tan2 20° − csc2 70°

Formula Used: csc(90° − A) = sec A; sec2 A − tan2 A = 1

⇒ Term 1: csc(65° + θ)

⇒ Term 2: sec(25° − θ) = sec(90° − (65° + θ)) = csc(65° + θ)

⇒ First half = csc(65° + θ) − csc(65° + θ) = 0

⇒ Term 3: tan2 20°

⇒ Term 4: csc2 70° = csc2 (90° − 20°) = sec2 20°

⇒ Second half = tan2 20° − sec2 20°

⇒ Using sec2 A − tan2 A = 1 ⇒ tan2 A − sec2 A = −1

⇒ Total Expression = 0 + (−1) = −1

∴ The correct answer is -1.

Additional Information

Complementary Angle Trigonometric Ratios

Pairs such as sin/cos, tan/cot, and sec/csc follow the rule: f(θ) = g(90° − θ). For example, sec θ = csc(90° − θ).

Standard Trigonometric Identities

Key identities include sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1, 1 + tan2 θ = sec2 θ, and 1 + cot2 θ = csc2 θ.

Sign Convention in Identities

Be careful with the order of subtraction: since sec2 θ − tan2 θ = 1, the reversed expression tan2 θ − sec2 θ always equals −1.

questions.question: The average of thirteen numbers is 47. The average of the first three numbers is 39 and that of the next seven numbers is 49. The 11 th number is two times the 12 th number and the 12th number is 3 less than the 13 th number. What is the average of 11 th and 13 th numbers?

The 11<sup>th</sup> number is two times the 12<sup>th</sup> number and the 12th number is 3 less than the 13<sup>th</sup> number. What is the average of 11<sup>th</sup> and 13<sup>th</sup> numbers?
questions.solution:
The average of thirteen numbers is 47

Sum of the thirteen numbers is 47 × 13 = 611

The average of first three number = 39

Sum of the first three number = 39 × 3 = 117

The average of next seven number = 49

Sum of next seven number = 49 × 7 = 343

Sum of last the three number = 611 – 117 – 343 = 151

Let 12th number be x

13th number = x + 3

questions.question: A person marks his goods x% above the cost price and allows a discount of 30% on the market price. If his profit is 5% then the value of x will be ∶
questions.questionHtml: A person marks his goods x% above the cost price and allows a discount of 30% on the market price. If his profit is 5% then the value of x will be ∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the net percentage change formula: Profit% = Mark-up% − Discount% − (Mark-up% × Discount%)/100.

Substitute the given values: 5 = x − 30 − (x × 30)/100.

5 + 30 = x − 0.3x

35 = 0.7x

x = 35 ÷ 0.7 = 50.

∴ The correct answer is 50.

Alternate Method

Given:

Mark-up percentage = x%

Discount percentage = 30%

Profit percentage = 5%

Formula used: CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)

Calculations:

⇒ CP / MP = (100 − 30) / (100 + 5)

⇒ CP / MP = 70 / 105

⇒ CP / MP = 2 / 3

⇒ Let CP = 2 units and MP = 3 units.

⇒ Mark-up = MP − CP = 3 − 2 = 1 unit.

⇒ Mark-up percentage (x) = (Mark-up / CP) × 100

⇒ x = (1 / 2) × 100

⇒ x = 50.

∴ The correct answer is 50.

Additional Information

CP, MP, and SP Relation

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is directly given by (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

Net Percentage Change

When a value is increased by a% (mark-up) and then decreased by b% (discount), the net change is a − b − (ab/100).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts d1% and d2% are given, the single equivalent discount is d1 + d2 − (d1 × d2)/100.

questions.question: The value of \(\frac{{{{\left( {253} \right)}^3}\; + \;{{\left( {247} \right)}^3}}}{{25.3\; \times \;25.3 - 624.91\; + \;24.7\; \times \;24.\;7}}\) is 50 × 10 k , where the value of k is ∶
questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\frac{{{{\left( {253} \right)}^3}\; + \;{{\left( {247} \right)}^3}}}{{25.3\; \times \;25.3 - 624.91\; + \;24.7\; \times \;24.\;7}}\)is 50 × 10k, where the value of k is ∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Recognize the identity: a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2).

Let a = 253 and b = 247. The denominator is scaled down by 102 = 100 compared to the numerator terms.

Value = (a + b) × 100 = (253 + 247) × 100 = 500 × 100 = 50000.

Given 50 × 10k = 50000 ⇒ 10k = 1000 = 103 ⇒ k = 3.

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Alternate Method

Given: (2533 + 2473) ÷ (25.3 × 25.3 − 624.91 + 24.7 × 24.7) = 50 × 10k

Formula Used: a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2)

⇒ Let a = 253 and b = 247

⇒ 25.3 = a/10 and 24.7 = b/10

⇒ 25.3 × 24.7 = (253 × 247) ÷ 100 = 62491 ÷ 100 = 624.91

⇒ Denominator = (a/10)2 − (ab/100) + (b/10)2 = (a2 − ab + b2) ÷ 100

⇒ Expression = [ (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2) ] ÷ [ (a2 − ab + b2) ÷ 100 ]

⇒ Expression = (a + b) × 100 = (253 + 247) × 100

⇒ 500 × 100 = 50000

⇒ 50 × 10k = 50000

⇒ 10k = 1000 = 103

⇒ k = 3

Additional Information

Algebraic Identities

a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2) and a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2).

Laws of Indices
