questions.question: If 5 sin θ – 4 cos θ = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of \(\frac{{5\sin \theta - 2\cos \theta }}{{5\sin \theta \; + \;3\cos \theta }}\) is ∶
questions.questionHtml: If 5 sin θ – 4 cos θ = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of \(\frac{{5\sin \theta - 2\cos \theta }}{{5\sin \theta \; + \;3\cos \theta }}\) is ∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given: 5 sin θ − 4 cos θ = 0 ⇒ 5 sin θ = 4 cos θ.

Directly substitute 4 cos θ in place of 5 sin θ in the required expression.

Value = (4 cos θ − 2 cos θ) ÷ (4 cos θ + 3 cos θ)

Value = 2 cos θ ÷ 7 cos θ = 2/7.

∴ The correct answer is 2/7.

Alternate Method

Given: 5 sin θ − 4 cos θ = 0, where 0° < θ < 90°.

Formula Used: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ.

⇒ 5 sin θ = 4 cos θ

⇒ sin θ / cos θ = 4/5

⇒ tan θ = 4/5

Expression = (5 sin θ − 2 cos θ) / (5 sin θ + 3 cos θ)

Divide the numerator and denominator by cos θ:

⇒ [(5 sin θ / cos θ) − (2 cos θ / cos θ)] / [(5 sin θ / cos θ) + (3 cos θ / cos θ)]

⇒ (5 tan θ − 2) / (5 tan θ + 3)

Substitute tan θ = 4/5:

⇒ (5 × (4/5) − 2) / (5 × (4/5) + 3)

⇒ (4 − 2) / (4 + 3)

⇒ 2/7

∴ The correct answer is 2/7.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Ratios

Standard ratios in a right triangle: sin θ = Perpendicular/Hypotenuse, cos θ = Base/Hypotenuse, and tan θ = Perpendicular/Base.

Quotient Identity

The ratio of sine to cosine is always equal to the tangent of that angle: tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ.

Pythagorean Identity

For any angle θ, sin2θ + cos2θ = 1. This allows conversion between sine and cosine values.

questions.question: If sin θ = √3cosθ, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of 2sin 2 θ + sec 2 θ + sinθsec θ + cosec θ is ∶
questions.questionHtml: If sin θ = √3cosθ, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of 2sin<sup>2</sup>θ + sec<sup>2</sup>θ + sinθsec θ + cosec θ is ∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given: sin θ = √3 cos θ ⇒ tan θ = √3.

For 0° < θ < 90°, tan θ = √3 ⇒ θ = 60°.

Substitute θ = 60° in the expression: 2 sin2(60°) + sec2(60°) + sin(60°)sec(60°) + cosec(60°).

Value = 2 × (3/4) + 4 + (√3/2 × 2) + 2/√3 = 3/2 + 4 + √3 + 2/√3.

Value = 11/2 + 5√3/3 = (33 + 10√3)/6.

∴ The correct answer is (33 + 10√3)/6.

Alternate Method

Given: sin θ = √3 cos θ and 0° < θ < 90°

Formula Used: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ; sin 60° = √3/2; sec 60° = 2; cosec 60° = 2/√3.

⇒ sin θ / cos θ = √3

⇒ tan θ = √3 ⇒ θ = 60°

⇒ Expression = 2sin2θ + sec2θ + sinθsecθ + cosecθ

⇒ Value = 2 × (sin 60°)2 + (sec 60°)2 + (sin 60° × sec 60°) + (cosec 60°)

⇒ Value = 2 × (√3/2)2 + (2)2 + (√3/2 × 2) + (2/√3)

⇒ Value = 2 × (3/4) + 4 + √3 + 2/√3

⇒ Value = 3/2 + 4 + √3 + 2/√3

⇒ Value = 11/2 + (√3 + 2/√3)

⇒ Value = 11/2 + (3 + 2)/√3 = 11/2 + 5/√3

⇒ Value = 11/2 + 5√3/3

⇒ Value = (33 + 10√3)/6

∴ The correct answer is (33 + 10√3)/6.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Ratios of 60°

sin 60° = √3/2, cos 60° = 1/2, tan 60° = √3, cot 60° = 1/√3, sec 60° = 2, cosec 60° = 2/√3.

Fundamental Identity

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1 | 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ | 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ.

Reciprocal Relations

cosec θ = 1/sin θ | sec θ = 1/cos θ | cot θ = 1/tan θ.

questions.question: The graphs of the equations 3x + y – 5 = 0 and 2x – y – 5 = 0 intersect at the point P(α, β). What is the value of (3α + β)?
questions.questionHtml: The graphs of the equations 3x + y – 5 = 0 and 2x – y – 5 = 0 intersect at the point P(α, β). What is the value of (3α + β)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The intersection point P(α, β) must satisfy both given equations.

The first equation is 3x + y − 5 = 0, which simplifies to 3x + y = 5.

Since P(α, β) lies on this line, we can substitute x = α and y = β.

Therefore, 3α + β = 5.

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Line 1: 3x + y − 5 = 0 ⇒ 3x + y = 5

Line 2: 2x − y − 5 = 0 ⇒ 2x − y = 5

Intersection point = P(α, β)

To find the intersection point P(α, β), solve the system of equations:

⇒ (3x + y) + (2x − y) = 5 + 5

⇒ 5x = 10

⇒ x = 2

Substitute x = 2 in the second equation:

⇒ 2(2) − y = 5

⇒ 4 − y = 5

⇒ y = 4 − 5 = −1

⇒ Point P(α, β) = (2, −1)

⇒ α = 2 and β = −1

Required value = 3α + β:

⇒ 3(2) + (−1)

⇒ 6 − 1 = 5

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Additional Information

Condition for Unique Solution

For a pair of linear equations a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 and a2x + b2y + c2 = 0, a unique solution exists if a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2.

Consistency of Equations

A system is consistent if it has at least one solution (intersecting or coincident lines) and inconsistent if it has no solution (parallel lines).

Slope-Intercept Form

Any linear equation can be represented as y = mx + c, where m is the slope and c is the y-intercept.

questions.question: \(\sqrt {\frac{{\cot \theta \; + \;\cos \theta }}{{\cot \theta - cos\theta }}} \) is equal to ∶
questions.questionHtml: \(\sqrt {\frac{{\cot \theta \; + \;\cos \theta }}{{\cot \theta - cos\theta }}} \) is equal to ∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume θ = 60°. Then &cot; 60° = 1/√3 and &cos; 60° = 1/2.

Expression = √[(1/√3 + 1/2) / (1/√3 − 1/2)] = √[(2 + √3) / (2 − √3)].

Rationalizing the denominator: √[(2 + √3)2 / (22 − (√3)2)] = √[(2 + √3)2 / 1] = 2 + √3.

Now check Option 4: sec 60° + tan 60° = 2 + √3. This matches the expression value.

For θ = 45°, Expression = √[(1 + 1/√2) / (1 − 1/√2)] = √2 + 1, and Option 4 = √2 + 1.

∴ The correct answer is sec θ + tan θ.

Alternate Method

Given: √ [(&cot; θ + &cos; θ) / (&cot; θ − &cos; θ)]

Formula Used: &cot; θ = &cos; θ / &sin; θ | 1 − &sin;2 θ = &cos;2 θ | &sec; θ = 1 / &cos; θ

Calculations:

⇒ Expression = √ [(&cos; θ / &sin; θ + &cos; θ) / (&cos; θ / &sin; θ − &cos; θ)]

⇒ Factor out &cos; θ: √ [(&cos; θ × (1 / &sin; θ + 1)) / (&cos; θ × (1 / &sin; θ − 1))]

⇒ Expression = √ [(&csc; θ + 1) / (&csc; θ − 1)]

⇒ Rationalizing: √ [(&csc; θ + 1)2 / (&csc;2 θ − 1)]

⇒ Using &csc;2 θ − 1 = &cot;2 θ: (&csc; θ + 1) / &cot; θ

⇒ Split terms: (&csc; θ / &cot; θ) + (1 / &cot; θ)

⇒ [(1 / &sin; θ) / (&cos; θ / &sin; θ)] + &tan; θ = 1 / &cos; θ + &tan; θ = &sec; θ + &tan; θ

∴ The correct answer is sec θ + tan θ.

Additional Information

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental relations like &sin;2θ + &cos;2θ = 1, 1 + &tan;2θ = &sec;2θ, and 1 + &cot;2θ = &csc;2θ are essential for simplifying radical expressions.

Rationalization Shortcut

For expressions of the form √[(1+&sin;θ)/(1−&sin;θ)], the result is always &sec;θ + &tan;θ. Similarly, √[(1−&sin;θ)/(1+&sin;θ)] results in &sec;θ − &tan;θ.

Reciprocal and Quotient Rules

Always convert complex terms like &cot;θ and &csc;θ into &sin;θ and &cos;θ to simplify the ratio easily.

questions.question: A circle is inscribed in ΔABC, touching AB, BC and AC at the points P, Q and R respectively. If AB - BC = 4 cm, AB - AC = 2 cm and the perimeter of ΔABC = 32 cm, then PB + AR is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: A circle is inscribed in ΔABC, touching AB, BC and AC at the points P, Q and R respectively. If AB - BC = 4 cm, AB - AC = 2 cm and the perimeter of ΔABC = 32 cm, then PB + AR is equal to∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By tangent properties from an external point, AP = AR and BP = BQ.

Therefore, the sum PB + AR = PB + AP = AB.

Let AB = x cm. Then BC = x − 4 cm and AC = x − 2 cm.

Perimeter = x + (x − 4) + (x − 2) = 32 cm.

3x − 6 = 32 ⇒ 3x = 38 ⇒ x = 38/3 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 38/3 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Circle touches AB at P, BC at Q, AC at R.

AB − BC = 4 cm

AB − AC = 2 cm

Perimeter of ΔABC = 32 cm

Formula Used:

Tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length.

Calculations:

Let AB = c, BC = a, and AC = b.

⇒ c − a = 4 ⇒ a = c − 4

⇒ c − b = 2 ⇒ b = c − 2

⇒ Perimeter = a + b + c = 32

⇒ (c − 4) + (c − 2) + c = 32

⇒ 3c − 6 = 32

⇒ 3c = 38 ⇒ c = 38/3 cm

So, AB = 38/3 cm.

From the property of tangents:

⇒ AP = AR

⇒ PB + AR = PB + AP

⇒ PB + AP = AB

⇒ PB + AR = 38/3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 38/3 cm.

Additional Information

Incircle Properties

The center of the inscribed circle (incenter) is the point of intersection of the internal angle bisectors of the triangle.

Semi-perimeter and Tangents

If s is the semi-perimeter, then the length of the tangents from the vertices are: AP = AR = s − a, BP = BQ = s − b, and CQ = CR = s − c.

Area of Triangle

Area of ΔABC = r × s, where r is the inradius and s is the semi-perimeter (a+b+c)/2.

questions.question: Chord AB of a circle is produced to a point P, and C is a point on that circle such that PC is a tangent to the circle. If PC = 18 cm, and BP = 15 cm, then AB is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: Chord AB of a circle is produced to a point P, and C is a point on that circle such that PC is a tangent to the circle. If PC = 18 cm, and BP = 15 cm, then AB is equal to∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the Tangent-Secant Theorem: (Tangent)2 = (Outside part of secant) × (Total length of secant).

PC2 = PB × PA

182 = 15 × (15 + AB)

324 = 15 × (15 + AB) ⇒ 15 + AB = 324 ÷ 15 = 21.6

AB = 21.6 − 15 = 6.6 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 6.6 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: Length of tangent PC = 18 cm and length of produced part BP = 15 cm.

Formula Used: When a secant PAB and a tangent PC are drawn from an external point P, then PC2 = PB × PA.

Let the length of chord AB be x cm.

⇒ Total length PA = PB + AB = 15 + x

⇒ According to the theorem: PC2 = PB × PA

⇒ 182 = 15 × (15 + x)

⇒ 324 = 225 + 15x

⇒ 324 − 225 = 15x

⇒ 99 = 15x

⇒ x = 99 ÷ 15

⇒ x = 6.6 cm

∴ The correct answer is 6.6 cm.

Additional Information

Internal Chord Intersection

If two chords AB and CD intersect at a point P inside the circle, then PA × PB = PC × PD.

External Secant Intersection

If two secants PAB and PCD intersect at a point P outside the circle, then PA × PB = PC × PD.

Alternate Segment Theorem

The angle between a tangent and a chord through the point of contact is equal to the angle in the alternate segment.

questions.question: If (√2 + √5 - √3) × k = - 12, then what will be the value of k?
questions.questionHtml: If (√2 + √5 - √3) × k = - 12, then what will be the value of k?
questions.solution:
Given:

(√2 + √5 - √3) × k = -12

Formula used:

(a + b)(a - b) = a2 - b2

(a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab

Calculation:

(√2 + √5 - √3) × k = -12

⇒ k = \(\dfrac{-12}{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{5} - \sqrt{3}}\)

⇒ k = \(\dfrac{-12 \times (\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3})}{(\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{5} - \sqrt{3})(\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3})}\)

⇒ k = \(\dfrac{-12 \times (\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3})}{(\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{5})^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2}\)

⇒ k = \(\dfrac{-12 \times (\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3})}{2 + 5 + 2\sqrt{10} - 3}\)

⇒ k = \(\dfrac{-12 \times (\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3})}{4 + 2\sqrt{10}}\)

⇒ k = \(\dfrac{-6 \times (\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3})}{2 + \sqrt{10}}\)

⇒ k = \(\dfrac{-6 \times (\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3}) \times (2 - \sqrt{10})}{(2 + \sqrt{10})(2 - \sqrt{10})}\)

⇒ k = \(\dfrac{-6 \times (\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3}) \times (2 - \sqrt{10})}{4 - 10}\)

⇒ k = \(\dfrac{-6 \times (\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3}) \times (2 - \sqrt{10})}{-6}\)

⇒ k = (√2 + √5 + √3)(2 - √10)

questions.question: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 4 cm, its surface area is increased by 464 π cm 2 What is the volume (in cm 3 ) of the original sphere?
questions.questionHtml: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 4 cm, its surface area is increased by 464 π cm<sup>2</sup> What is the volume (in cm<sup>3</sup>) of the original sphere?
questions.solution:
Let the radius of sphere be r cm.

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr3

Total surface area of sphere = 4πr2

If the radius increased by 4 cm, then new radius = (r + 4) cm

New surface area of sphere = 4π(r + 4)2

According to the question

4π(r + 4)2 - 4πr2 = 464π

⇒ 4π[(r + 4)2 - r2] = 464π

⇒ r2 + 16 + 8r - r2 = 464π/4π = 116

⇒ 8r = 116 - 16 = 100

⇒ r = 100/8 = 25/2

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr3 = (4/3) × (25/2)3 × π = (4/3) × (15625/8) × π = 15625π/6

questions.question: In ΔABC, ∠A = 58°. If I is the in-centre of the triangle, then the measure of ∠BIC is∶
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, ∠A = 58°. If I is the in-centre of the triangle, then the measure of ∠BIC is∶

Shortcut Trick

Angle at the in-centre (I) is always given by: ∠BIC = 90° + (∠A ÷ 2)

Given ∠A = 58°

⇒ ∠BIC = 90° + (58° ÷ 2)

Given:

In ΔABC, ∠A = 58°

I is the in-centre of the triangle.

Formula Used:

In any triangle, the angle formed by the internal bisectors of two angles at the in-centre is 90° plus half of the third angle: ∠BIC = 90° + ∠A/2

Calculations:

⇒ ∠A = 58°

⇒ ∠BIC = 90° + (∠A ÷ 2)

⇒ ∠BIC = 90° + (58° ÷ 2)

⇒ ∠BIC = 90° + 29°

⇒ ∠BIC = 119°

∴ The correct answer is 119°.

Additional Information

In-centre Properties

The in-centre is the intersection of the internal angle bisectors. The radius of the in-circle (r) = Area ÷ semi-perimeter (s).

Circumcentre Angle

If O is the circumcentre of ΔABC, then the angle ∠BOC = 2 × ∠A.

Orthocentre Angle

If H is the orthocentre of ΔABC, then the angle ∠BHC = 180° − ∠A.

Ex-centre Angle

If Ie is the ex-centre opposite to vertex A, then the angle ∠BIeC = 90° − (∠A ÷ 2).

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows 28% discount on the marked price of an article and still makes a profit of 20% If he gains Rs. 30.80 on the sale of one article, then what will be the cost price of the article?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper allows 28% discount on the marked price of an article and still makes a profit of 20% If he gains Rs. 30.80 on the sale of one article, then what will be the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Profit % = 20%

Actual Profit = ₹30.80

20% of CP = 30.80

Cost Price (100% of CP) = 30.80 × 5 = ₹154

∴ The correct answer is ₹154.

Alternate Method

Given:

Discount = 28% of Marked Price

Profit % = 20%

Profit Amount = ₹30.80

Formula:

Profit = Profit % × Cost Price (CP)

Cost Price (CP) = (Profit ÷ Profit %) × 100

Calculation:

⇒ Profit = 20% of Cost Price

⇒ ₹30.80 = (20 ÷ 100) × CP

⇒ ₹30.80 = (1 ÷ 5) × CP

⇒ CP = 30.80 × 5

⇒ CP = ₹154.00

∴ The correct answer is ₹154.

Additional Information

Cost Price and Marked Price Relationship

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount %) ÷ (100 + Profit %). This ratio is extremely useful when both discount and profit percentages are provided to find the CP or MP directly.

Mark-up Percentage

Mark-up % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. It represents how much higher the marked price is set above the cost price.

Discount Amount

Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price. Note that profit and loss are always calculated on CP (unless specified otherwise), while discount is always calculated on MP.

questions.question: In quadrilateral ABCD, the bisectors of ∠A and ∠B meet at O and ∠AOB = 64°. ∠C + ∠D is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: In quadrilateral ABCD, the bisectors of ∠A and ∠B meet at O and ∠AOB = 64°. ∠C + ∠D is equal to∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a quadrilateral, the angle formed by the bisectors of two adjacent angles is equal to half the sum of the remaining two angles.

Property: ∠AOB = (∠C + ∠D) ÷ 2

64° = (∠C + ∠D) ÷ 2

∠C + ∠D = 64° × 2 = 128°

∴ The correct answer is 128°.

Alternate Method

Given: In quadrilateral ABCD, AO and BO are the bisectors of ∠A and ∠B respectively. ∠AOB = 64°.

In ΔAOB, the sum of internal angles is 180°:

⇒ ∠OAB + ∠OBA + ∠AOB = 180°

⇒ ∠OAB + ∠OBA + 64° = 180°

⇒ ∠OAB + ∠OBA = 180° − 64° = 116°

Since AO and BO are angle bisectors:

⇒ (1/2)∠A + (1/2)∠B = 116°

⇒ ∠A + ∠B = 2 × 116° = 232°

For quadrilateral ABCD, the sum of internal angles is 360°:

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ 232° + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ ∠C + ∠D = 360° − 232° = 128°

∴ The correct answer is 128°.

Additional Information

Angle Sum Property of Quadrilaterals

The sum of all four interior angles of a convex quadrilateral is always 360°.

Adjacent Angle Bisectors Theorem

In any quadrilateral, the angle between the bisectors of two adjacent angles is equal to half the sum of the remaining two angles: ∠AOB = (∠C + ∠D) ÷ 2.

Opposite Angle Bisectors

The angle between the bisectors of two opposite angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the absolute difference of the other two angles.

questions.question: An article is sold at a certain price. If it is sold at \(33\frac{1}{3}\% \) of the price, there is a loss of \(33\frac{1}{3}\%\) What is the percentage profit when it is sold at 60% of the original selling price?
questions.questionHtml: An article is sold at a certain price. If it is sold at \(33\frac{1}{3}\% \) of the price, there is a loss of \(33\frac{1}{3}\%\) What is the percentage profit when it is sold at 60% of the original selling price?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let original selling price SP1 = 300 units.

New SP = 33 1/3% of 300 = 1/3 × 300 = 100 units.

Loss of 33 1/3% means New SP = 2/3 of CP ⇒ 100 = 2/3 CP ⇒ CP = 150 units.

Required SP = 60% of 300 = 180 units.

Profit = 180 − 150 = 30 units ⇒ Profit% = (30/150) × 100 = 20%.

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Case 1: New Selling Price = 33 1/3% of Original SP; Loss = 33 1/3%.

Case 2: Target Selling Price = 60% of Original SP.

Formula: SP = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss%)/100

Let the original Selling Price be SP1.

⇒ Case 1 SP = (1/3)SP1

⇒ Loss = 33 1/3% = 1/3

⇒ SP = CP × (1 − Loss) ⇒ (1/3)SP1 = CP × (1 − 1/3)

⇒ (1/3)SP1 = CP × (2/3)

⇒ SP1 = 2 CP

⇒ Target Selling Price (SP2) = 60% of SP1

⇒ SP2 = 0.6 × (2 CP) = 1.2 CP

⇒ Profit = SP2 − CP = 1.2 CP − CP = 0.2 CP

⇒ Profit % = (0.2 CP / CP) × 100 = 20%

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Additional Information

Fraction and Percentage Conversion

Standard fractions like 33 1/3% = 1/3 and 66 2/3% = 2/3 simplify calculations involving profit and loss ratios significantly.

Profit and Loss on Cost Price

Unless stated otherwise, profit or loss percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP). Profit% = (SP − CP)/CP × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), while the final transaction result (Profit/Loss) is measured against the CP.

questions.question: If x 8 - 1442x 4 +1 = 0, then a possible value of x - 1/x is∶
questions.questionHtml: If x<sup>8</sup> - 1442x<sup>4 </sup>+1 = 0, then a possible value of x - 1/x is∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Divide the equation by x4 to get x4 + 1/x4 = 1442.

Using the rule: if x4 + 1/x4 = k, then x2 + 1/x2 = √(k + 2).

x2 + 1/x2 = √(1442 + 2) = √1444 = 38.

Then, x − 1/x = √(38 − 2) = √36 = 6.

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Alternate Method

Given: x8 − 1442x4 + 1 = 0

Formula Used: (a − b)2 = a2 + b2 − 2ab and (a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab

⇒ x8 + 1 = 1442x4

⇒ x4 + 1/x4 = 1442 (Dividing both sides by x4)

⇒ (x2 + 1/x2)2 − 2 × x2 × (1/x2) = 1442

⇒ (x2 + 1/x2)2 = 1442 + 2 = 1444

⇒ x2 + 1/x2 = √1444 = 38

⇒ (x − 1/x)2 + 2 × x × (1/x) = 38

⇒ (x − 1/x)2 = 38 − 2 = 36

⇒ x − 1/x = √36 = 6

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identity for Squares

x2 + 1/x2 = (x + 1/x)2 − 2 or x2 + 1/x2 = (x − 1/x)2 + 2.

Higher Power Transformation

To go from xn + 1/xn = k to xn/2 + 1/xn/2, use √(k + 2); to go to xn/2 − 1/xn/2, use √(k − 2).

Standard Square Roots

It is helpful to remember common squares: 382 = 1444, 372 = 1369, 362 = 1296.

questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, AB = 6 cm, AC = 8 cm, and BC = 9 cm. The length of the median AD is∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply Apollonius Theorem directly: AB2 + AC2 = 2(AD2 + (BC/2)2)

Substitute the given values: 62 + 82 = 2(AD2 + 4.52)

100 = 2(AD2 + 20.25) ⇒ 50 = AD2 + 20.25

AD2 = 29.75 = 119/4

AD = √119 / 2 cm

∴ The correct answer is √119/2 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: AB = 6 cm, AC = 8 cm, BC = 9 cm

Formula Used: Apollonius's Theorem: AB2 + AC2 = 2(AD2 + BD2), where D is the midpoint of BC.

⇒ BC = 9 cm, so BD = DC = 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5 cm

⇒ By Apollonius Theorem: AB2 + AC2 = 2(AD2 + BD2)

⇒ 62 + 82 = 2(AD2 + 4.52)

⇒ 36 + 64 = 2(AD2 + 20.25)

⇒ 100 = 2(AD2 + 20.25)

⇒ 50 = AD2 + 20.25

⇒ AD2 = 50 − 20.25 = 29.75

⇒ AD2 = 119 ÷ 4

⇒ AD = √119 ÷ 2 cm

∴ The correct answer is √119/2 cm.

Additional Information

Sum of Squares of Medians

In any triangle, 3 × (sum of squares of sides) = 4 × (sum of squares of medians). i.e., 3(AB2 + BC2 + CA2) = 4(AD2 + BE2 + CF2).

Centroid Property

The centroid (G) of a triangle divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1 from the vertex. AG : GD = 2 : 1.

Median in Right-Angled Triangle

The length of the median to the hypotenuse is exactly half the length of the hypotenuse.

questions.question: When the price of an item was reduced by 25% then its sale was increased by x%. If there is an increase of 20% in the receipt of the revenue, then the value of x will be∶
questions.questionHtml: When the price of an item was reduced by 25% then its sale was increased by x%. If there is an increase of 20% in the receipt of the revenue, then the value of x will be∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Revenue = Price × Sale

Price Ratio = 100 : 75 = 4 : 3

Revenue Ratio = 100 : 120 = 5 : 6

Sale Ratio = (Revenue Ratio ÷ Price Ratio) = (5/4) : (6/3) = 1.25 : 2

Percentage increase in sale (x) = [(2 − 1.25) ÷ 1.25] × 100 = (0.75 ÷ 1.25) × 100 = 60

∴ The correct answer is 60.

Alternate Method

Given: Price reduction = 25%, Revenue increase = 20%, Sale increase = x%.

Formula: Revenue = Price × Sale

Let initial Price = 100 and initial Sale = 100.

⇒ Initial Revenue = 100 × 100 = 10000

⇒ New Price = 100 − 25% of 100 = 75

⇒ New Revenue = 10000 + 20% of 10000 = 12000

⇒ New Sale = New Revenue ÷ New Price

⇒ New Sale = 12000 ÷ 75 = 160

⇒ Increase in Sale = New Sale − Initial Sale = 160 − 100 = 60

⇒ Percentage increase (x) = (60 ÷ 100) × 100 = 60

∴ The correct answer is 60.

Additional Information

Net Percentage Change Formula

If two variables change by a% and b%, the net effect on their product is (a + b + ab/100)%. Here, −25 + x + (−25x/100) = 20.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by x% and then y%, the final value is Initial × (1 + x/100) × (1 + y/100).

Fractional Conversions

25% = 1/4 (Reduction factor = 3/4) and 20% = 1/5 (Increase factor = 6/5). Multiplying factor for sale = (6/5) ÷ (3/4) = 8/5 = 1.6.

questions.question: In a school, 4/9 of the number of students are girls and the rest are boys. 3/5 of the number of boys are below 12 years of age and 5/12 of the number of girls are 12 years or above 12 years of age. If the number of students below 12 years of age is 480, then 5/18 of the total number of students in the school will be equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: In a school, 4/9 of the number of students are girls and the rest are boys. 3/5 of the number of boys are below 12 years of age and 5/12 of the number of girls are 12 years or above 12 years of age. If the number of students below 12 years of age is 480, then 5/18 of the total number of students in the school will be equal to∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the total number of students be 180 units (LCM of 9, 5, and 12 is 180).

Girls = 4/9 × 180 = 80; Boys = 180 − 80 = 100.

Boys < 12 years = 100 × 3/5 = 60; Girls < 12 years = 80 × (1 − 5/12) = 80 × 7/12 = 140/3.

Total students < 12 years = 60 + 140/3 = 320/3 units = 480 ⇒ 1 unit = 4.5.

Value of 5/18 of total = 5/18 × 180 units = 50 units = 50 × 4.5 = 225.

∴ The correct answer is 225.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of girls = 4/9 of total

Ratio of boys = 1 − 4/9 = 5/9 of total

Boys < 12 years = 3/5 of boys

Girls ≥ 12 years = 5/12 of girls ⇒ Girls < 12 years = 7/12 of girls

Total students below 12 years = 480

Let total students be x.

⇒ Total students below 12 years = (3/5 × 5/9 x) + (7/12 × 4/9 x) = 480

⇒ (1/3)x + (7/27)x = 480

⇒ (9x + 7x) / 27 = 480

⇒ 16x / 27 = 480

⇒ x = (480 × 27) / 16

⇒ x = 30 × 27 = 810

Now, finding 5/18 of total students:

⇒ Value = 5/18 × 810

⇒ Value = 5 × 45 = 225

∴ The correct answer is 225.

Additional Information

LCM Method for Fractions

To avoid working with complex fractions, assume the total quantity as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of all the denominators present in the problem.

Complementary Fractions

If a fraction a/b is given for one part, the remaining part is always 1 − (a/b) = (b − a)/b. For example, if 5/12 are ≥ 12 years, then 1 − 5/12 = 7/12 are < 12 years.

Fraction Multiplication Rule

To find a fraction of a fraction (e.g., 3/5 of 5/9 of total), multiply the numerators together and the denominators together: (3 × 5) / (5 × 9) = 1/3.

questions.question: \(\frac{{\left( {2\sin A} \right)\left( {1 + \sin A} \right)}}{{1 + \sin A + \cos A}}\) is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: \(\frac{{\left( {2\sin A} \right)\left( {1 + \sin A} \right)}}{{1 + \sin A + \cos A}}\) is equal to∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Pick a specific value for angle A to test the options. Let A = 90°.

Then sin 90° = 1 and cos 90° = 0.

Expression = [2(1)(1 + 1)] ÷ (1 + 1 + 0) = 4 ÷ 2 = 2.

Check options: (1) 1+0=1; (2) 1+1−0=2; (3) 1−0=1; (4) 1+0−1=0.

Only Option (2) gives the result 2.

∴ The correct answer is 1 + sin A − cos A.

Alternate Method

Given: Expression = [2 sin A (1 + sin A)] ÷ [1 + sin A + cos A]

⇒ Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 + sin A − cos A).

⇒ Denominator = [(1 + sin A) + cos A] × [(1 + sin A) − cos A]

⇒ Denominator = (1 + sin A)2 − cos2A

⇒ Denominator = 1 + sin2A + 2 sin A − (1 − sin2A)

⇒ Denominator = 1 + sin2A + 2 sin A − 1 + sin2A

⇒ Denominator = 2 sin2A + 2 sin A = 2 sin A (1 + sin A)

⇒ Expression = [2 sin A (1 + sin A) × (1 + sin A − cos A)] ÷ [2 sin A (1 + sin A)]

⇒ Expression = 1 + sin A − cos A

∴ The correct answer is 1 + sin A − cos A.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identity: sin2A + cos2A = 1, which implies cos2A = 1 − sin2A and sin2A = 1 − cos2A.

Conjugate Multiplication

To simplify fractions with (a+b+c) in the denominator, group terms as ((a+b)+c) and multiply by ((a+b)−c) to use the difference of squares: (x+y)(x−y) = x2 − y2.

Value Substitution Method

Standard angles like 0°, 45°, and 90° are useful for checking trigonometric identities quickly, provided the expression is defined for those values.
